summary: Betts–Stix's finiteness theorem for Selmer sections (Annals 2025): for a number field K with no CM subfield and a smooth projective curve Y/K of genus at least 2, the image of the Selmer sections of Grothendieck's fundamental exact sequence in Y(K_v) is finite for every finite place v (Theorem A), and so is the projection of the finite descent locus (Theorem B). SPM.0 defines Selmer sections and their localisations and states the Harari–Stix description of finite descent; SPM.1 attaches to each section the symplectic pair of an abelian-by-finite family and shows that Selmer sections localise into the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus (Theorem 7.1). SPM.2 and SPM.3 supply the local and global numerics: filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules with their automorphism groups and the orbit lemma, and self-conjugate places with the average Hodge–Tate weight of pure representations. SPM.4 and SPM.5 prove, without models, that v-adic period maps control the (φ, N, G_v)-modules of the fibres (Theorems 3.22 and 3.3, Proposition 4.11), through Scholze's relative comparison and Shimizu's horizontal semistability. SPM.6 defines S-good pairs and the Lawrence–Venkatesh loci and proves the principal trichotomy; SPM.7 and SPM.8 show the type (a) and (b) loci finite under full monodromy and the type (c) locus empty for a suitable Kodaira–Parshin family; SPM.9 assembles Theorem 6.5, the Mordell conjecture, the self-conjugate Selmer finiteness, Theorem A and Theorem B. The section conjecture and Stoll's conjecture are named propositions only; Theorem A's no-CM hypothesis is kept and used only through self-conjugacy.

nodes.title: Restriction of Galois sections to decomposition groups
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with algebraic closure K̄, X a geometrically connected separated K-scheme of finite type, u a place of K (finite or archimedean) and ι: K̄ → K̄_u a K-embedding into an algebraic closure of the completion K_u, with ι^*: G_u = Gal(K̄_u/K_u) → G_K the induced injection onto the decomposition group D_u (R01.2). Fix a geometric point x̄_u of X_{K̄_u} and its image x̄ in X_{K̄}. Then the natural maps give an isomorphism of profinite extensions of G_u: π₁^ét(X_{K_u}, x̄_u) ≅ π₁^ét(X, x̄) ×_{G_K} G_u, restricting to the isomorphism π₁^ét(X_{K̄_u}, x̄_u) ≅ π₁^ét(X_{K̄}, x̄) of IG.1/charzero-base-extension on geometric kernels. Consequently, for a continuous section s: G_K → π₁^ét(X, x̄) of the fundamental exact sequence, the map σ ↦ (s(ι^*σ), σ) is a continuous section s|G_u of 1 → π₁^ét(X_{K̄_u}) → π₁^ét(X_{K_u}) → G_u → 1. Conjugating s by an element of the geometric kernel conjugates s|G_u by its image, so restriction descends to a map res_u: Sect(X/K) → Sect(X_{K_u}/K_u) of the section classes of NC.6/section-classes. A second embedding ι' changes res_u by the canonical base-point bijection of NC.6/section-classes, and res_u ∘ κ_X = κ_{X_{K_u}} ∘ (X(K) → X(K_u)) for the section maps κ of NC.6/section-class-map.
hypotheses: K is a number field, so the characteristic is zero and the base-extension theorem IG.1/charzero-base-extension applies to every connected finite-type K-scheme.
X is geometrically connected, so the fundamental exact sequences over K and over K_u are exact (IG.1).
At a complex place G_u is trivial and res_u has a one-point target; at a real place G_u has order two.
proofSteps: Compare the two exact sequences: π₁^ét(X_{K_u}) maps to π₁^ét(X) compatibly with ι^*: G_u → G_K, so it maps to the fibre product π₁^ét(X) ×_{G_K} G_u; both are extensions of G_u, by π₁^ét(X_{K̄_u}) and by π₁^ét(X_{K̄}), and the map on kernels is the isomorphism of IG.1/charzero-base-extension, so the five lemma for profinite groups gives the isomorphism (Harari–Stix, Introduction, p. 2).
A section s defines the section σ ↦ (s(ι^*σ), σ) of the fibre product; transport it through the isomorphism of the first step.
If t = δsδ⁻¹ with δ in the geometric kernel, then t|G_u is the conjugate of s|G_u by the image of δ in π₁^ét(X_{K̄_u}); so res_u is well defined on classes.
For x ∈ X(K), the section s_x comes from functoriality of π₁ for Spec K → X; composing with Spec K_u → Spec K gives the section of the image point, by functoriality of π₁ for Spec K_u → Spec K → X.

Changing ι to ι ∘ σ, or to τ ∘ ι with τ ∈ G_u, changes ι^* by conjugation (R01.2(iii)); the induced change of base point is an étale path, which acts on classes by the canonical bijection of NC.6/section-classes.
acceptance: For X = Spec K both section sets are points and res_u is the unique map.
For X = G_{m,K} with reference sections at 1, res_u is the restriction map H¹(K, Ẑ(1)) → H¹(K_u, Ẑ(1)), which under Kummer theory is induced by K^× → K_u^×.

sources.match: Restricting a section of the fundamental exact sequence (1.1) to a decomposition group G_u gives a splitting of the local fundamental exact sequence of Y over K_u.

In characteristic zero the comparison theorem identifies π₁ of the base change to a field extension with the fibre product of π₁ over the absolute Galois group, so a global section induces a section of each local sequence.

nodes.title: Injectivity of the section map over p-adic fields
nodes.statement: Let L be a finite extension of Q_p and X a geometrically connected L-variety that admits an immersion into an abelian variety over L (for instance a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g ≥ 1 with X(L) ≠ ∅, through its Abel–Jacobi map). Then the section map κ_X: X(L) → Sect(X/L) is injective. In particular, for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve Y of genus ≥ 1 over a number field K, a finite place u of K and a class c ∈ Sect(Y_{K_u}/K_u), at most one y ∈ Y(K_u) has κ(y) = c.
hypotheses: L is a finite extension of Q_p (a local field of characteristic zero); the statement fails over ℝ, where the torus A(ℝ)⁰ is divisible and κ only sees the connected component of a real point.
proofSteps: Apply the field-general first assertion of NC.6/section-map-injective (Stix, Appendix B, Proposition 44 and Theorem 45), rather than its number-field corollary: it suffices that every abelian variety A/L has no nonzero rational point divisible by every positive integer.

A(L) is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group: it is closed in a projective space over L, which is compact and totally disconnected; so A(L) is a profinite abelian group (Stix, Appendix B, Remark 46, which gives compactness as the reason).

For every open subgroup U of A(L), the quotient A(L)/U is finite of some exponent e_U, so an element divisible by e_U lies in U; an element divisible by every n therefore lies in every open subgroup, and the open subgroups of a profinite group intersect in 0.

For a curve of genus ≥ 1 with an L-point b, the Abel–Jacobi map at b is a closed immersion into the Jacobian (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions §6.4, as cited by NC.6/section-map-injective); if X(L) = ∅ there is nothing to prove.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over Q_p with full 2-torsion, the four 2-torsion points have pairwise distinct section classes.
Over ℝ the analogous map is not injective: two distinct real points on the same connected component of E(ℝ) give the same section class.

sources.locator: Appendix B, Theorem 45 and Remark 46, p. 22
sources.match: Injectivity of the section map holds over any field whose abelian varieties have no nonzero divisible rational points; the remark notes that local fields qualify by compactness.
The localisation map loc_u is defined by sending a Selmer section to the unique K_u-point that gives its restriction; uniqueness is this injectivity.

nodes.title: Selmer sections and the localisation maps
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and X a geometrically connected separated K-scheme of finite type. A section class c ∈ Sect(X/K) is Selmer if, for every place u of K, archimedean places included, res_u(c) lies in the image of the local section map κ_{X_{K_u}}: X(K_u) → Sect(X_{K_u}/K_u) (SPM.0/local-section-restriction, NC.6/section-class-map). The Selmer sections form the subset Sec^Sel(X/K) ⊆ Sect(X/K). When κ_{X_{K_u}} is injective at a finite place u (SPM.0/local-section-map-injective: for instance X a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 1), the localisation map loc_u: Sec^Sel(X/K) → X(K_u) sends c to the unique y_u ∈ X(K_u) with κ(y_u) = res_u(c). The definition and loc_u do not depend on the embeddings ι chosen at the places.
hypotheses: X is geometrically connected, so Sect(X/K) is defined (NC.6/section-classes).
The Selmer condition is imposed at every place, the real and complex places included; at a complex place it is automatic when X(ℂ) ≠ ∅.
loc_u is defined only at finite places, where the local section map is injective; at a real place a section class determines at most a connected component of X(K_u).
proofSteps: Define Sec^Sel(X/K) as the intersection over all places u of the preimages res_u⁻¹(κ_{X_{K_u}}(X(K_u))).
At a finite place, SPM.0/local-section-map-injective makes the point y_u with κ(y_u) = res_u(c) unique, which defines loc_u.
Independence of ι: two embeddings change res_u by the canonical base-point bijection, which is compatible with κ_{X_{K_u}} (NC.6/section-class-map), so the Selmer condition and y_u do not change.
For x ∈ X(K), res_u(κ_X(x)) = κ_{X_{K_u}}(x) by SPM.0/local-section-restriction, so κ_X(X(K)) ⊆ Sec^Sel(X/K) and loc_u(κ_X(x)) = x.
acceptance: Every rational point gives a Selmer section; for a curve of genus ≥ 1 it localises to itself at every finite place.
If X(K_u) = ∅ for some place u, then Sec^Sel(X/K) = ∅.
Under Grothendieck's section conjecture (NC.6/section-conjecture), Sec^Sel(Y/K) = Sect(Y/K) = κ_Y(Y(K)) for a smooth projective curve of genus ≥ 2.

sources.match: A section is Selmer when its restriction to every decomposition group is the section of a local point; Sec^Sel(Y/K) is the set of such sections and loc_u sends a Selmer section to that local point at a finite place u.

sources.match: The section conjecture predicts that all sections come from rational points, which the Selmer condition imitates locally.

nodes.title: Modified adelic points and the finite descent locus
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and X a smooth projective geometrically connected K-variety, so that X(A_K) = ∏_u X(K_u) (RP.2/adelic-points-general). The modified adelic points are X(A_K)_• := ∏_{u finite} X(K_u) × ∏_{u | ∞} π₀(X(K_u)), with the projection X(A_K) → X(A_K)_• that replaces each archimedean component by its connected component. For a torsor f: Z → X under a finite étale K-group scheme G, a point P ∈ X(A_K)_• survives (Z, G) if it is the image of a point of Z^ξ(A_K)_• for some twist ξ ∈ H¹(K, G). The finite descent locus X(A_K)_•^{f-cov} is the set of P ∈ X(A_K)_• surviving every such torsor. It is the image of the finite étale descent set X(A_K)^{ét} of RP.3/descent-set under the projection, it contains the image of X(K), and Stoll's Main Conjecture 9.1 (every smooth projective curve is 'very good': the abelian finite descent locus is the closure of X(K)) implies that it equals the closure of the image of X(K) for curves; that prediction is a named proposition and is never assumed.
hypotheses: X smooth projective and geometrically connected over a number field.
Only torsors under finite étale group schemes enter; torsors under connected groups give other descent sets.
proofSteps: Form X(A_K)_• as the stated product, with the product topology; the projection from X(A_K) is surjective.
Define survival through the twists of the torsor, as in Stoll, Definition 5.2, and the locus as in Stoll, Definition 5.4(1).

Comparison with RP.3/descent-set: a point of X(A_K) lies in X(A_K)^{ét} exactly when its image survives every finite étale torsor. At a real place the map Z^ξ(K_u) → X(K_u) is a finite covering map, so its image is open and closed and is a union of connected components; hence lifting a component is the same as lifting each of its points.
X(K) maps into the locus by the descent theorem: a rational point lies in the image of the rational points of exactly one twist (Stoll, Theorem 5.1).
acceptance: For X = P¹_K the locus is all of X(A_K)_•, since P¹ is geometrically simply connected (Stoll, Lemma 5.8(1)).
For a smooth projective curve of genus ≥ 2, the projection of the locus to X(K_v) at a finite place v is the set studied in Betts–Stix, Theorem B.

sources.match: Modified adelic points: the archimedean factors are replaced by their sets of connected components, with the surjection from the adelic points.
A modified adelic point survives a torsor under a finite étale group scheme when it lifts to some twist; the finite descent locus is the set of points surviving all such torsors.

For a geometrically simply connected variety the locus is everything; the Main Conjecture says every curve is very good (closure of the rational points = abelian descent locus), which forces the finite descent locus to be that closure too.
Recalls the modified adelic points, the finite descent locus, its containment of the rational points and Stoll's conjecture that it equals them.

nodes.title: Harari–Stix: finite descent and Galois sections
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and X a smooth projective geometrically connected K-variety. (a) An adelic point (P_u)_u ∈ X(A_K) lies in the finite étale descent set X(A_K)^{ét} (RP.3/descent-set) if and only if there is a section class c ∈ Sect(X/K) with res_u(c) = κ_{X_{K_u}}(P_u) for every place u of K. (b) Consequently, if X is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 1 and v is a finite place, the projection of X(A_K)_•^{f-cov} (SPM.0/modified-finite-descent-locus) to X(K_v) equals loc_v(Sec^Sel(X/K)).
hypotheses: X smooth projective geometrically connected over a number field; in (a) every place of K, archimedean ones included, is used (the case S = ∅ of Harari–Stix).
In (b), loc_v is defined because the local section map is injective at finite places (SPM.0/local-section-map-injective).
proofSteps: (a) is Harari–Stix, Theorem 2.1, equivalence (i) ⇔ (iii), with S = ∅ and U trivial. A torsor under a finite group scheme G gives an evaluation map on local sections; survival of (P_u) means the local evaluations come from H¹(K, G). Inverse limits over the finite quotients of π₁, with the nonempty-limit argument of Harari–Stix Proposition 1.1, produce a global section; Chebotarev's density theorem supplies the hypothesis (**) of their Corollary 1.7.

(b), ⊆: lift a point of X(A_K)_•^{f-cov} to X(A_K) by choosing real points in the given components; by the component argument of SPM.0/modified-finite-descent-locus the lift lies in X(A_K)^{ét}. Then (a) gives c with res_u(c) = κ(P_u) at every place, so c is Selmer and loc_v(c) = P_v.

(b), ⊇: for a Selmer class c choose P_u with κ(P_u) = res_u(c) at every place (P_u = loc_u(c) at finite places). By (a) the adelic point (P_u) lies in X(A_K)^{ét}, and its image lies in X(A_K)_•^{f-cov}.
acceptance: Under (b), Theorem A (finiteness of loc_v(Sec^Sel)) is equivalent to the finiteness of the projection of the finite descent locus to X(K_v): this is Betts–Stix, Theorem B.
For X(K) ≠ ∅ the diagonal image of a rational point corresponds to its own section in (a).

sources.locator: Theorem 2.1 and its proof, Remarks (1) and (4), pp. 11–12
sources.match: For an adelic point with local points everywhere outside a density-zero set, surviving every descent by finite group schemes is equivalent to the local sections coming from one global section; the proof translates Corollary 1.7 using Chebotarev.
The formal criterion: a compatible system of local sections comes from a global section exactly when it survives every finite descent obstruction, given a density hypothesis.
Cites Harari–Stix (as [HS12, Theorem 11]) for the identification of the finite descent locus with the image of the Selmer sections under the total localisation map.

nodes.title: Symplectic modules and symplectic pairs
nodes.statement: Let C be one of the Q_p-linear tensor categories below, with its underlying-module realisations: the continuous Q_p-representations of a profinite group G, the filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules of SPM.2/restriction-induction, or the Q_p-local systems on a scheme. An algebra in C is a commutative unital algebra object A; for G-representations, a finite-dimensional commutative Q_p-algebra with a continuous G-action by algebra automorphisms. A symplectic A-module in C is a triple (V, L, ω) with V an A-module in C that is finite locally free over A, L an A-module in C free of rank one over A, and ω: ∧²_A V → L a morphism in C that is A-linear and perfect (it induces V ≅ Hom_A(V, L)). A symplectic pair is (A, V) with V a symplectic A-module (L and ω understood); a morphism (A, V) → (A′, V′) is a triple of morphisms f_A: A → A′ of algebras, f_V: V → V′ and f_L: L → L′ in C, compatible with the module structures (f_V(av) = f_A(a)f_V(v), and likewise for f_L) and with the pairings (f_L ∘ ω = ω′ ∘ ∧²f_V). SP(C) is the category of symplectic pairs and π₀SP(C) its set of isomorphism classes. For G-representations, Σ_A := Hom_{Q_p-alg}(A, Q_p) is a finite set with a continuous right G-action; for ψ ∈ Σ_A with stabiliser G_ψ, V_ψ := Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V is a symplectic representation of G_ψ with similitude line L_ψ.
hypotheses: For G-representations, A is a finite-dimensional commutative Q_p-algebra, possibly non-reduced or non-split, and Σ_A consists of its Q_p-points only, not its Q̄_p-points. In MF(φ,N,G_v), the corresponding finite algebras are over the realisation fields Q_p^nr and K_v.
V is finite locally free over A, of constant rank 2d when A is connected; L is free of rank one.

The definition is internal to C; finiteness, local freeness and the rank of the line are checked on its underlying coefficient modules. A Q_p-valued neutral fibre functor is not assumed for MF(φ, N, G_v): its de Rham realisation is K_v-valued and its potentially semistable realisation is Q_p^nr-valued.
proofSteps: Take ∧²_A V in C using the symmetric monoidal structure and the A-module structure; perfectness is a condition on the underlying A-modules.
Base change along ψ: A → Q_p preserves perfectness, giving (V_ψ, L_ψ, ω_ψ) with an action of G_ψ.

If A = ∏_{ψ∈Σ} Q_p is split and Σ is one G-orbit with base point ψ₀, then V ≅ ∏_ψ V_ψ and V = Ind_{G_{ψ₀}}^{G} V_{ψ₀} as symplectic modules over A = Ind_{G_{ψ₀}}^G Q_p (structure of modules over artinian rings, as in the proof of Betts–Stix Proposition 6.7).

The tensor functors used here, compatible with the underlying-module realisations (restriction, coefficient extension, and D_pH), preserve finite locally free modules, rank-one lines and perfect alternating pairings. A fully faithful such functor reflects isomorphism classes of pairs.
acceptance: An elliptic curve E over K gives (Q_p, H¹_ét(E_{K̄}, Q_p)) with the Weil pairing to Q_p(−1).
A split algebra A = Q_p × Q_p with G acting by the swap gives V = Ind V_ψ as in the proof step.

sources.match: A symplectic module over an algebra in a tensor category is a locally free module with a perfect alternating pairing to a rank-one module; symplectic pairs form a category, defined in any tensor category; the cohomology of a fibre of an abelian-by-finite family is the basic example.
Σ_A is the finite set of Q_p-algebra maps A → Q_p with its Galois action, and V_ψ the base change along ψ, a symplectic representation of the stabiliser.
A symplectic Galois representation is a triple (V, L, ω) with L one-dimensional and ω a perfect equivariant alternating pairing.

D_pH sends symplectic pairs of de Rham representations to symplectic pairs of filtered (φ, N, G_v)-modules
a Galois section gives a symplectic pair of G_K-representations

nodes.title: The symplectic pair of a fibre
nodes.statement: Let X → Y′ → Y be an abelian-by-finite family (LV.2/abelian-by-finite-family) over a scheme Y of characteristic zero with polarisation λ, F a field and y ∈ Y(F). Then H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,F̄}, Q_p) := (H⁰_ét(X_{y,F̄}, Q_p), H¹_ét(X_{y,F̄}, Q_p)), with the pairing ω_λ^ét: ∧² over H⁰_ét of H¹_ét → H⁰_ét(−1) of the polarisation, is a symplectic pair of continuous G_F-representations (SPM.1/symplectic-pair). Its algebra H⁰_ét(X_{y,F̄}, Q_p) = H⁰_ét(Y′_{y,F̄}, Q_p) = ∏_{Y′_y(F̄)} Q_p is split, with Σ = Y′_y(F̄) as a G_F-set, and its fibre at the point ψ given by y′ ∈ Y′_y(F̄) is H¹_ét of the abelian variety X_{y′} over F(y′). Isomorphisms of families over Y induce isomorphisms of pairs, and the construction commutes with field extension F ⊆ F′.
hypotheses: The family has constant relative dimension d > 0 over Y′, so H¹_ét has constant rank 2d over H⁰_ét.
char F = 0, so étale cohomology with Q_p coefficients behaves as in LV.2 and the decomposition over Y′_y(F̄) holds.
proofSteps: Decompose X_y = ⊔_{y′} X_{y′} over the closed points of Y′_y; H^•_ét(X_{y,F̄}) = ∏_{y′} Ind_{G_{F(y′)}}^{G_F} H^•_ét(X_{ȳ′}) as algebras (Betts–Stix (4.1)).
The polarisation pairing on each H¹_ét(X_{ȳ′}) (LV.1/abelian-variety-cohomology-properties(d)) assembles to the H⁰_ét-linear perfect pairing of Lemma 4.2, requested from LV.2 in the model-free form.
Functoriality and base change follow from those of étale cohomology and of the Chern class of the Poincaré bundle.
acceptance: For Y′ = Y (a polarised abelian scheme) the algebra is Q_p and the pair is (Q_p, H¹_ét(X_{ȳ}, Q_p)) with the polarisation pairing.
Σ = Y′_y(F̄) is the G_F-set whose orbits are the closed points of Y′_y (Betts–Stix Remark 6.6).

sources.match: For a point of the base, the étale cohomology of the fibre in degrees ≤ 1 is a symplectic pair: H⁰ is an algebra, H¹ a symplectic module over it through the polarisation, and the cohomology decomposes as a product of inductions over the closed points of Y′_y.
H⁰ of the fibre is the split algebra of functions on the geometric points of Y′_y, so its Q_p-points are Y′_y(F̄).

uses.how: the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus compares H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v}) with the restriction of a global pair
the fibres of the relative symplectic pair are these pairs

nodes.title: The relative symplectic pair R^{≤1}π_*Q_p
nodes.statement: Let π: X → Y′ → Y be an abelian-by-finite family over a normal connected scheme Y of characteristic zero, with polarisation λ. Then R^•π_*Q_p ≅ ∧^• over π_*Q_p of R¹π_*Q_p as Q_p-local systems on Y_ét. The relative Chern class c₁^ét(λ)/Y := ½ c₁^ét((1, λ)^*P)/Y ∈ H⁰(Y, R²π_*Q_p(1)) is defined as the image of the class of a line bundle under H¹(X, G_m) → H⁰(Y, R¹π_*G_m) → H⁰(Y, R²π_*Z_p(1)) → H⁰(Y, R²π_*Q_p(1)) (Leray, then the limit of Kummer boundaries). It induces a perfect pairing ω_λ: ∧² over π_*Q_p of R¹π_*Q_p → π_*Q_p(−1), so R^{≤1}π_*Q_p := (π_*Q_p, R¹π_*Q_p) is a symplectic pair of Q_p-local systems on Y_ét. Its fibre at a geometric point ȳ is the pair H^{≤1}_ét(X_ȳ, Q_p) of SPM.1/fibre-symplectic-pair, compatibly with the Galois action when ȳ lies over a point with values in a field.
hypotheses: Y normal and connected, so Q_p-local systems are continuous representations of π₁^ét(Y) (IG.0/adic-representations).
π smooth proper, so the higher direct images are local systems compatible with base change.
proofSteps: The isomorphism ∧^• R¹ → R^• is checked on geometric fibres, where it is the cohomology of abelian varieties.
Construct c₁^ét(L)/Y: Leray low-degree terms H¹(X, G_m) → H⁰(Y, R¹π_*G_m), then the Kummer boundaries R¹π_*G_m → R²π_*μ_{p^n}, compatible in n, then tensor with Q_p.
The fibre of c₁^ét(λ)/Y at ȳ is c₁^ét(λ_ȳ), by functoriality of the Leray sequence; the induced pairing is perfect on every fibre by the étale part of the LV.2 request, hence perfect.
The pair of the fibre is H^{≤1}_ét(X_ȳ, Q_p) by proper base change.
acceptance: For Y′ = Y = Spec F the relative pair is the pair of SPM.1/fibre-symplectic-pair with its G_F-action.
The rank of R¹π_*Q_p over π_*Q_p is 2d.

sources.match: The relative étale cohomology of an abelian-by-finite family is a local system with R^• the exterior algebra on R¹ over π_*Q_p; the relative Chern class of the polarisation, built from the Leray and Kummer sequences, gives a perfect pairing whose fibres are those of the fibres.

uses.how: its π₁-representations are restricted along a Galois section

nodes.title: The symplectic pair attached to a Galois section
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, X → Y′ → Y an abelian-by-finite family and η̄ a geometric point of Y_{K̄}. Let (A, V) be the symplectic pair of continuous π₁^ét(Y, η̄)-representations corresponding to R^{≤1}π_*Q_p (SPM.1/relative-symplectic-pair, IG.0/adic-representations). For a continuous section s: G_K → π₁^ét(Y, η̄), (A_s, V_s) is (A, V) with G_K acting through s: a symplectic pair of G_K-representations. Conjugating s by γ ∈ π₁^ét(Y_{K̄}, η̄) gives an isomorphic pair (the action of γ is a G_K-equivariant isomorphism), and changing η̄ along an étale path gives an isomorphic pair; so the isomorphism class [A_s, V_s] ∈ π₀SP(Rep_{Q_p}(G_K)) depends only on the class of s in Sect(Y/K).
hypotheses: Y geometrically connected, so the fundamental exact sequence is exact and sections are defined (NC.6/section-classes).
The family is fixed; its pair is a pair of π₁^ét(Y)-representations.
proofSteps: Restrict the π₁^ét(Y)-actions on A and V along s; the algebra, module, line and pairing structures are π₁-equivariant, so they remain G_K-equivariant.
For s′ = γsγ⁻¹, the action of γ on A and V intertwines the two restricted actions and preserves all structures.
For another base point, an étale path γ conjugates the fundamental exact sequences (Betts–Stix (†) of §7.2); its action identifies the pairs for s and γsγ⁻¹.
acceptance: For y ∈ Y(K) and its section s_y, (A_{s_y}, V_{s_y}) ≅ H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p) (the case u = global of SPM.1/sections-restrict-local-systems).
The class map Sect(Y/K) → π₀SP(Rep_{Q_p}(G_K)) is well defined.

sources.match: A section restricts the π₁-representations of the relative cohomology to G_K, giving a symplectic pair whose isomorphism class depends only on the conjugacy class of the section and not on the base point.

uses.how: the pair (A_s, V_s) of a Selmer section is the interpolating pair of Definition 6.1
any v-adic obstruction from a Q_p-local system is transported to sections the same way

nodes.title: Local systems restricted along sections at local points
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a geometrically connected variety, 𝕃 a Q_p-local system on Y_ét with π₁^ét(Y, η̄)-representation ρ, u a place of K and y_u ∈ Y(K_u). If c ∈ Sect(Y/K) satisfies res_u(c) = κ_{Y_{K_u}}(y_u), then for any representative s of c the G_u-representation (ρ ∘ s)|G_u (restriction along ι^*: G_u → G_K) is isomorphic to the fibre 𝕃_{ȳ_u} at the geometric point over y_u with its G_u-action. The isomorphism is compatible with tensor products, duals and morphisms of local systems; in particular it carries algebra, module and pairing structures to the same structures.
hypotheses: The place u may be archimedean; the statement uses only res_u(c) = κ(y_u).
The isomorphism depends on the choice of a path from η̄ to ȳ_u, which changes it by an inner automorphism compatible with all structures.
proofSteps: Choose the base point at ȳ_u by an étale path; this replaces s by a conjugate and ρ by an isomorphic representation (SPM.1/section-symplectic-pair).

With this base point, κ(y_u) is represented by π₁(Spec K_u) → π₁(Y_{K_u}, ȳ_u) → π₁(Y, ȳ_u), induced by the morphism of pointed schemes (Spec K_u, Spec K̄_u) → (Y_{K_u}, ȳ_u) (SPM.0/local-section-restriction).

By the definition of π₁ as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, pulling 𝕃 back along this morphism is the representation of G_u on the fibre 𝕃_{ȳ_u}; so (ρ ∘ s)|G_u is the fibre (Betts–Stix, proof of Proposition 7.2).
All constructions are functorial in 𝕃, so they respect tensor products and morphisms.
acceptance: For u the global field itself (a rational point y and s = s_y) the statement gives (ρ ∘ s_y) ≅ 𝕃_ȳ as G_K-representations.
The same argument, applied to a finite étale cover Z → Y (a local system of finite sets, not stated in the source), gives the G_u-set of geometric points of the fibre Z_{y_u}.

sources.match: Any v-adic obstruction to rational points coming from a Q_p-local system on Y constrains the image of loc_v on Selmer sections, by restricting the corresponding π₁-representation along the section.

If the restriction of a section to G_u is the section of a local point, the restricted representations of the relative cohomology are the cohomology of the fibre at that point, by choosing the base point there and using the definition of π₁.

nodes.title: The pair of a section interpolates its local points
nodes.statement: Let K, Y and X → Y′ → Y be as in SPM.1/section-symplectic-pair, s a section and u a place of K. If res_u[s] = κ(y_u) for y_u ∈ Y(K_u), then (A_s|G_u, V_s|G_u) ≅ H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_u,K̄_u}, Q_p) as symplectic pairs of G_u-representations.
hypotheses: As in SPM.1/sections-restrict-local-systems; the pairing structure is carried by the isomorphism because ω_λ is a morphism of local systems.
proofSteps: Apply SPM.1/sections-restrict-local-systems to π_*Q_p and R¹π_*Q_p and to the pairing ω_λ.
The fibre of R^{≤1}π_*Q_p at ȳ_u is H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_u,K̄_u}, Q_p) by SPM.1/relative-symplectic-pair.
acceptance: For a Selmer section s, the pair (A_s, V_s) has the local restriction H^{≤1}_ét(X_{loc_u(s)}) at every finite place u.

sources.match: The restriction of the pair of a section to a decomposition group is the pair of the fibre at the local point whose section is the restricted section.

nodes.title: The adelic Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, X → Y′ → Y an abelian-by-finite family and p a prime. The adelic Lawrence–Venkatesh locus Y(A_K)^LV_X ⊆ Y(A_K) = ∏_u Y(K_u) is the set of adelic points (y_u)_u for which some symplectic pair (A, V) of continuous Q_p-representations of G_K satisfies H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_u,K̄_u}, Q_p) ≅ (A|G_u, V|G_u) as symplectic pairs of G_u-representations for every place u; such (A, V) interpolates (y_u). For a p-adic place v, Y(K_v)^LV_X is the projection of Y(A_K)^LV_X to Y(K_v).
hypotheses: All places of K are used, the archimedean ones included; restriction to G_u is through the embedding fixed at u (R01.2/local-restriction), and the condition does not depend on it.
proofSteps: Both sides of each condition are pairs of G_u-representations (SPM.1/fibre-symplectic-pair, R01.2/local-restriction); isomorphism of symplectic pairs is that of SPM.1/symplectic-pair.
Changing the embedding at u conjugates the restriction by an element of G_K, which is an isomorphism of pairs; so the condition is independent of choices.

nodes.title: Filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules: restriction and induction
nodes.statement: Let K_v be a finite extension of Q_p inside a fixed algebraic closure K̄_v, Q_p^nr ⊆ K̄_v the maximal unramified extension of Q_p and G_v = Gal(K̄_v/K_v). A (φ, N, G_v)-module is a finite-dimensional Q_p^nr-space D with a bijective Frobenius-semilinear φ, a Q_p^nr-linear N with Nφ = pφN, and a semilinear G_v-action commuting with φ and N; it is discrete when stabilisers of vectors are open. A filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-module is a triple D = (D_pst, D_dR, c_BO) with D_pst a discrete (φ, N, G_v)-module, D_dR a finite-dimensional K_v-space with an exhaustive separated decreasing filtration F^•, and c_BO: K̄_v ⊗_{Q_p^nr} D_pst ≅ K̄_v ⊗_{K_v} D_dR a G_v-equivariant isomorphism; with the evident morphisms and tensor products these form the ⊗-category MF(φ, N, G_v). It is equivalent to the colimit over finite Galois L/K_v of the filtered (φ, N, Gal(L/K_v))-modules of R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules-with-descent-data. For de Rham V, D_pH(V) := (D_pst(V), D_dR(V), c_BO) (R06.3/plan/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module), and for a smooth proper K_v-variety X, H^•_pH(X/K_v) := (D_pst(H^•_ét(X_{K̄_v}, Q_p)), H^•_dR(X/K_v), c_dR ∘ c_BO) with Scholze's c_dR (P8/de-rham-pair-pushforward-compatibilities). For a finite extension L_w/K_v in K̄_v with G_w ≤ G_v: restriction D|G_w := (D_pst|G_w, L_w ⊗_{K_v} D_dR, c_BO) is a ⊗-functor MF(φ, N, G_v) → MF(φ, N, G_w); induction Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} D := (Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} D_pst, D_dR viewed over K_v, c′_BO), with Ind D_pst = Map_{G_w}(G_v, D_pst) carrying the induced φ and N, the Q_p^nr-structure (λψ)(g) = g(λ)ψ(g), and c′_BO the composite of Ind(c_BO) with K̄_v ⊗ Ind ≅ Ind(K̄_v ⊗ −) and Ind(K̄_v ⊗_{L_w} D_dR) ≅ K̄_v ⊗_{K_v} D_dR (built from the trace-form idempotent of L_w ⊗_{K_v} L_w), is a lax ⊗-functor right adjoint to restriction. For a smooth proper K_v-variety X, H^•_pH(X_{L_w}/L_w) ≅ H^•_pH(X/K_v)|G_w (2.1), and for a smooth proper L_w-variety X viewed over K_v, H^•_pH(X/K_v) ≅ Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} H^•_pH(X/L_w) (2.2).
hypotheses: K_v/Q_p finite; all extensions L_w are taken inside the fixed K̄_v.
B_st is identified with its image in B_dR independently of a choice of p-adic logarithm, following Shimizu (Betts–Stix footnote 4).
Induction follows the convention Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} W = Map_{G_w}(G_v, W) with (g·ψ)(h) = ψ(hg).
proofSteps: Define the category and its tensor product componentwise; the comparison c_BO forces D_pst to be discrete.

The equivalence with descent data: for D_pst discrete, D_pst = Q_p^nr ⊗_{L_0} D_pst^{G_L} for L large enough, and D_dR = (L ⊗ D_pst^{G_L})^{Gal(L/K_v)}; this is the colimit description stated in R06.2/plan/filtered-phi-n-modules-with-descent-data.
For de Rham V, D_pst(V) has full dimension by the p-adic monodromy theorem (R06.3/plan/p-adic-monodromy-theorem) and c_BO is an isomorphism (R06.3/plan/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module).
Restriction: restrict the G_v-action and extend scalars of D_dR; c_BO is unchanged after identifying K̄_v ⊗_{K_v} D_dR = K̄_v ⊗_{L_w} (L_w ⊗ D_dR).

Induction: the twisted scalar action makes Ind D_pst a Q_p^nr-space; φ and N act pointwise and commute with G_v; c′_BO sends 1 ⊗ ψ to Σ_i (g_i ⊗ 1)(e·c_BO(ψ(g_i⁻¹))) over coset representatives g_i, with e = Σ_j x_j ⊗ y_j for dual bases of L_w under the trace form. The adjunction is Frobenius reciprocity, and the lax ⊗-structure is the one induced by the ⊗-structure of restriction.

(2.1) follows from H_ét((X_{L_w})_{K̄_v}) = H_ét(X_{K̄_v}), L_w ⊗ H_dR(X/K_v) ≅ H_dR(X_{L_w}/L_w) and base-change compatibility of c_dR (CohomologyComparisons CP.6/naturality-base-change-and-cup-products); (2.2) follows from Shapiro's identification H_ét(X_{K̄_v}) ≅ Ind H_ét(X_{L̄_w}) and the adjunction.
acceptance: For the unit object 1 = (Q_p^nr, K_v, id), Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} 1 = H⁰_pH(Spec L_w/K_v), the algebra of functions on Hom_{K_v}(L_w, K̄_v).
D_pH(V|G_w) = D_pH(V)|G_w and D_pH(Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} V) ≅ Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} D_pH(V) for de Rham V.

sources.match: A (φ, N, G_v)-module is a Q_p^nr-space with semilinear bijective Frobenius, linear monodromy with Nφ = pφN, and a commuting semilinear G_v-action; a filtered discrete one adds a filtered K_v-space and a G_v-equivariant comparison over K̄_v; they form a tensor category.

D_pst(V) is the colimit of the semistable invariants over open subgroups, of full dimension for de Rham V by Berger; with D_dR and the Berthelot–Ogus-type comparison it gives D_pH(V), and D_pH is a fully faithful tensor functor on de Rham representations.

nodes.title: Automorphism groups and retwisted filtrations
nodes.statement: Let D be a (φ, N, G_v)-module (SPM.2/restriction-induction). Its endomorphism algebra End(D) is the Q_p-algebra of Q_p^nr-linear maps D → D commuting with φ, N and G_v, and Aut(D) is the functor on Q_p-algebras R ↦ the group of R ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p^nr-linear automorphisms of R ⊗_{Q_p} D commuting with 1 ⊗ φ, 1 ⊗ N and G_v, that is R ↦ (R ⊗_{Q_p} End(D))^×; it is represented by the unit group scheme of the finite-dimensional algebra End(D). For a symplectic (φ, N, G_v)-module (D, L, ω) (L of dimension one, ω: ∧²D → L perfect and equivariant), Aut^GSp(D) is the closed subgroup of Aut(D) × G_m whose R-points are pairs (f,c) satisfying ω(fx,fy) = cω(x,y); the factor c is part of the data even when D = 0. The scalar maps are λ ↦ λ id in Aut(D) and λ ↦ (λ id,λ²) in Aut^GSp(D), and have central image. For a filtered discrete module D = (D_pst, D_dR, c_BO), Aut(D_pst) acts on Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} GL(D_dR) by transporting 1 ⊗ ψ through c_BO and taking G_v-invariants, hence on Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} G, where G is the flag variety of filtrations of D_dR with the dimension data of F^•; for Φ ∈ G(K_v), M(Φ) := (D_pst, D_dR with the filtration Φ, c_BO).
hypotheses: K_v/Q_p finite; the similitude factor is recorded so that the degenerate case D = 0 behaves (Betts–Stix footnote 6).
proofSteps: First establish finite-dimensionality of End(D), before constructing the group scheme: the Frobenius descent/trace argument given in the first three proof steps of SPM.2/automorphism-dimension-bound proves that Q_p^nr ⊗ End(D) → End_{Q_p^nr}(D) is injective, using only the φ and G_v structures. It therefore bounds dim End(D) by (dim D)². Then represent Aut(D) by the unit group of this finite-dimensional algebra (Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layers 0 and 3). The later dimension theorem records the estimates for these already constructed groups; algebraicity does not depend on that theorem.

Inside Aut(D) × G_m impose the bilinear equations ω(fx,fy) = cω(x,y). These define a closed subgroup scheme with multiplication (f,c)(g,d) = (fg,cd). The projection to Aut(D) is a closed immersion when D ≠ 0; when D = 0 it is the map G_m → 1.

For ψ ∈ Aut(D_pst)(R), the R ⊗ K̄_v-linear map 1 ⊗ ψ on R ⊗ K̄_v ⊗ D_pst ≅ R ⊗ K̄_v ⊗ D_dR is G_v-equivariant, so its G_v-invariants give an R ⊗ K_v-linear automorphism of R ⊗ D_dR, not necessarily filtered (Betts–Stix Remark 2.14). This is an action on Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} GL(D_dR), hence on Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} of the flag variety (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1/flag-bundle, Weil restriction A6).
M(Φ) is again a filtered discrete module: only the filtration changed.
acceptance: For the unit object, End = Q_p and Aut = G_m.
M(F^•) = D for the original filtration F^•.

nodes.title: The orbit lemma for retwisted filtrations
nodes.statement: Let D = (D_pst, D_dR, c_BO) be a filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-module and G the flag variety of filtrations of D_dR with the dimension data of its filtration. For Φ₁, Φ₂ ∈ G(K_v), M(Φ₁) ≅ M(Φ₂) as filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules if and only if Φ₁ and Φ₂ lie in one Aut(D_pst)(Q_p)-orbit for the action of SPM.2/automorphism-group. Consequently the set of Φ with M(Φ) in a fixed isomorphism class lies in a closed Q_p-subvariety of Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} G of dimension at most dim_{Q_p} Aut(D_pst), and the same holds for finitely many classes. The symplectic version, with Aut^GSp(D_pst) acting on the Lagrangian Grassmannian of a symplectic D_dR, holds with the same proof.
hypotheses: The orbit statement is over Q_p-points; the dimension bound is for the Zariski closure of an orbit of an algebraic group acting algebraically.
proofSteps: An isomorphism M(Φ₁) → M(Φ₂) is determined by its D_pst-component, a (φ, N, G_v)-automorphism ψ of D_pst, because the D_dR-component is forced by c_BO.
That this ψ respects the filtrations says exactly that ψ carries Φ₁ to Φ₂ under the action of Remark 2.14.
An orbit of an algebraic group H acting algebraically on a variety has Zariski closure of dimension ≤ dim H; finitely many orbits likewise.
LV.4/filtered-phi-orbit is the special case of filtered φ-modules over an unramified base; the argument is the same.
acceptance: For K_v = Q_p and D_dR of dimension two with jumps {0, 1} and Aut(D_pst) = G_m² acting on P¹ through the eigenbasis, the orbits are the two eigenlines and their complement: three isomorphism classes of retwists.

sources.match: Two retwisted modules are isomorphic exactly when the filtrations are in one orbit of the Q_p-points of Aut(D_pst), so a fixed isomorphism class sweeps out a subvariety of dimension at most dim Aut(D_pst).

nodes.title: Dimension bounds for automorphism groups
nodes.statement: (1) For a (φ, N, G_v)-module D of Q_p^nr-dimension d, End(D) is a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra, the natural map Q_p^nr ⊗_{Q_p} End(D) → End_{Q_p^nr}(D) is injective, Aut(D) is an affine algebraic group over Q_p, and dim_{Q_p} Aut(D) ≤ d². (2) For a symplectic (φ, N, G_v)-module (D, L, ω) of rank 2d, Aut^GSp(D) is an affine algebraic group over Q_p of dimension ≤ d(2d + 1) + 1, the dimension of GSp_{2d}.
hypotheses: The injectivity uses both the G_v-action and the Frobenius φ: the G_v-action alone gives only traces to K_{v,0} (the extraction's E2).
proofSteps: Let ψ₁, …, ψ_k ∈ End(D) be Q_p-linearly independent and λ_i ∈ Q_p^nr with Σλ_iψ_i = 0 in End_{Q_p^nr}(D).
G_v-equivariance of the ψ_i gives Σσ(αλ_i)ψ_i = 0 for α ∈ Q_p^nr and σ ∈ G_v; G_v acts on Q_p^nr through Gal(Q_p^nr/K_{v,0}) only.

Since the ψ_i commute with φ, which is semilinear for the Frobenius of Q_p^nr, conjugating by φ gives ΣFrob(λ_i)ψ_i = 0. Frobenius and the image of G_v generate a dense subgroup of Gal(Q_p^nr/Q_p); averaging over a finite quotient through which the λ_i and α are fixed gives Σtr(αλ_i)ψ_i = 0 for the normalised trace to Q_p, so λ_i = 0 by non-degeneracy of the trace form (repair of the printed argument, extraction E2).
So End(D) has Q_p-dimension ≤ d², Aut(D) is its unit group scheme, and the injection induces a closed immersion Aut(D)_{Q_p^nr} → GL_{Q_p^nr}(D), whence dim Aut(D) ≤ d².

(2): after base extension to Q_p^nr, Aut^GSp(D) embeds in the group of pairs (f,c) in GL(D) × G_m satisfying ω(fx,fy) = cω(x,y). For d > 0 this is GSp_{2d}, of dimension d(2d + 1) + 1. For d = 0 it is G_m, of dimension 1, so the same formula holds with the retained-factor convention.
acceptance: For d = 1 (a rank-one module), dim Aut(D) ≤ 1; equality for D = 1.
For d = 1 in the symplectic case the bound is 4 = dim GL₂ = dim GSp₂.

sources.match: Automorphism groups of (φ, N, G_v)-modules are algebraic of dimension at most d², and the symplectic ones at most d(2d + 1) + 1, via an injection of Q_p^nr ⊗ End(D) into the linear endomorphisms.
The bounds are what the generalised Lawrence–Venkatesh argument needs on automorphism groups of symplectic (φ, N, G_v)-modules.

nodes.title: Conjugate and self-conjugate places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field. Two finite places v, v′ of K are conjugate if, for every CM subfield E ⊆ K, the restrictions v|_E and v′|_E are exchanged by the complex conjugation c_E of E, that is v′|_E = c_E(v|_E); v is self-conjugate if it is conjugate to itself. (1) If K has no CM subfield (for instance K totally real or of odd degree), every finite place is self-conjugate. (2) If K has a CM subfield, it has a largest one E_K (LV.1/largest-cm-subfield); then v, v′ are conjugate exactly when v′|_{E_K} = c_{E_K}(v|_{E_K}), and v is self-conjugate exactly when c_{E_K} fixes v|_{E_K}, i.e. the place of the maximal totally real subfield below v is inert or ramified in E_K. (3) The friendly places of Lawrence–Venkatesh (LV.1/friendly-place) are exactly the self-conjugate places unramified over Q.
hypotheses: K a number field; places are finite places (height-one primes of O_K).
Conjugacy is tested on every CM subfield, not only on E_K; by (2) the two tests agree.
proofSteps: (1) is vacuous: there is no E to test.

(2): a compositum of CM subfields of K is CM, so every CM subfield E lies in E_K and c_E is the restriction of c_{E_K}; restricting places from E_K to E commutes with conjugation, so the condition at E_K implies it at every E.
For the reformulation, c_{E_K} fixes a place of E_K exactly when that place is the only one above its restriction to E_K⁺, i.e. the restriction is inert or ramified.
(3): compare with LV.1/friendly-place; unramified over Q excludes the ramified case of (2).
acceptance: Over Q every place is self-conjugate; over Q(i) the place (3) is self-conjugate and friendly, (1 + i) is self-conjugate but not friendly, and the two places above 5 are conjugate to each other and not self-conjugate.

sources.match: Places are conjugate when their restrictions to every CM subfield are exchanged by complex conjugation, self-conjugate when conjugate to themselves; without a CM subfield every place is self-conjugate, with one the condition is at the maximal CM subfield, and friendly places are the self-conjugate places unramified over Q.
Self-conjugacy is slightly weaker than friendliness; with no CM subfield every finite place is self-conjugate, which is why Theorem A needs that hypothesis.

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate weights of pure characters at conjugate places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, p a prime and χ: G_K → Q_p^× a continuous character that is unramified and pure of weight n ∈ Z outside a finite set of places (R34.1/pure-and-integral-galois-representations) and de Rham at every place above p. For a place v | p let r_v be the Hodge–Tate weight of χ|G_v, the integer r with (C_p(r) ⊗ χ|G_v)^{G_v} ≠ 0, equivalently the filtration jump of D_dR(χ|G_v). If v and v′ above p are conjugate (SPM.3/self-conjugate-place), then r_v + r_{v′} = n. In particular, at a self-conjugate place v above p, n is even and r_v = n/2.
hypotheses: χ takes values in Q_p^×. With Q̄_p^×-values the statement is false when K has a CM subfield: for K = Q(i), p ≡ 3 mod 4 and v = (p), the character of G_K on V_p of the CM curve y² = x³ − x composed with an embedding Q_{p²} → Q̄_p is pure of odd weight 1 and de Rham at v (extraction item /24, red-team finding RT-PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/2).
Hodge–Tate weights are normalised so that Q_p(1) has weight −1.
proofSteps: Fix ι_p: Q̄ → Q̄_p and put m(τ) := r_{v(τ)} for embeddings τ: K → Q̄, where v(τ) is the place above p induced by ι_p ∘ τ.

Global purity gives m(c ∘ τ) + m(τ) = n for every complex conjugation c (LV.1/pure-character-conjugation-relation; Betts–Stix argue instead with class field theory and the Serre torus, using that the algebraic part of the associated Hecke character takes Q_p^×-values).
By LV.1/infinity-type-factorization, m(τ) depends only on τ|_{E_K}, and is the constant n/2 if K has no CM subfield.
For conjugate v, v′, pick τ with v(τ) = v; adjusting by the decomposition group of ι_p, pick τ′ with v(τ′) = v′ and τ′|_{E_K} = (c ∘ τ)|_{E_K}. Then r_{v′} = m(τ′) = m(c ∘ τ) = n − r_v.
For v self-conjugate take v′ = v.
acceptance: χ = χ_cyc⁻¹ (the representation Q_p(−1)) is pure of weight 2 and has Hodge–Tate weight 1 = 2/2 at every place above p.
A finite-order character has n = 0 and r_v = 0 everywhere.

sources.match: For a Q_p^×-valued character unramified and pure of weight n outside a finite set and de Rham above p, Hodge–Tate weights at conjugate places add up to n, so they equal n/2 at self-conjugate places; the proof uses global class field theory and Serre's description of the Serre torus.
Conventions: Hodge–Tate weight r means (C_p(r) ⊗ V)^{G_v} ≠ 0, and local Artin maps send uniformisers to arithmetic Frobenius.

nodes.title: Pure characters at self-conjugate places
nodes.statement: Let χ: G_K → Q_p^× be as in SPM.3/conjugate-places-weights and v a self-conjugate place above p. Then χ|G_v = χ₀ · χ_cyc^{−n/2} with χ₀ a character of G_v of finite order. If K has no CM subfield, χ · χ_cyc^{n/2} is itself of finite order on G_K.
hypotheses: χ is Q_p^×-valued; for the Q̄_p^×-valued CM character of SPM.3/conjugate-places-weights, χ|G_v is a Lubin–Tate character and n is odd.
proofSteps: Replacing χ by χ · χ_cyc^{n/2} (n is even by SPM.3/conjugate-places-weights), reduce to n = 0.

No CM subfield: r_u = 0 at every u | p, so the associated idele class character is finitely ramified at every place (LV.1/de-rham-character-locally-algebraic); it factors through a ray class group, which is finite, so χ has finite order (GlobalNumberFields Layers 2 and 7, with ClassFieldTheory Layer 11 for the Galois–idele character dictionary).

CM case: put E = E_K. The infinity-type factorisation of LV.1 gives an algebraic character on E whose composite with N_{K/E} is the algebraic local type of the weight-zero idele character η of K. Realise a positive power of that type by a Q_p-valued idele class character θ of E: choose a modulus on whose global units the algebraic character is trivial, define the character on principal ideals, and raise to an exponent killing the finite ray class group to extend it to all ideals without extracting roots in Q_p. Consequently η^m/(θ ∘ N_{K/E}) has trivial algebraic type at p and finite ramification everywhere, hence finite order by global class field theory. This finite-power norm descent is part of this target’s proof, not an assertion that restriction of η to A_E isolates one local component.

Conjugate infinity types of θ add to zero, so θθ̄ is finitely ramified everywhere and has finite order. At the self-conjugate prime v₀ = v|_E its local type is zero, so θ_{v₀} has finite image on units. For a uniformiser π, conjugation sends π to πu for a unit u. Thus θ_{v₀}(π)² differs from (θθ̄)_{v₀}(π) by a finite-order unit value, so θ_{v₀} has finite order on E_{v₀}^×. The norm descent then makes η_v^m finite order, hence η_v and χ|G_v finite order.
acceptance: For χ = χ_cyc⁻¹, χ|G_v = χ_cyc^{−1} with χ₀ = 1 and n = 2.

sources.match: At a self-conjugate place a pure de Rham Q_p^×-valued character is a finite-order character times a power of the cyclotomic character; the argument reduces to weight zero and uses finiteness of ray class groups, with an extra step through the maximal CM subfield.

nodes.title: Average Hodge–Tate weight at a self-conjugate place
nodes.statement: Let L/K be a finite extension of number fields, V a continuous Q_p-representation of G_L that is de Rham at every place of L above p and unramified and pure of weight n outside a finite set, and v a self-conjugate place of K above p. Then Σ_{w | v} [L_w : K_v] Σ_{i∈Z} i·dim_{L_w} gr^i_F D_dR,w(V) = n·[L : K]·dim_{Q_p}(V)/2, where D_dR,w(V) := D_dR(V|G_w). Equivalently, the average Hodge–Tate weight of Ind_{G_L}^{G_K}V at v (the filtration weight of LV.1/filtration-weight) is n/2.
hypotheses: v is self-conjugate on K; no condition is put on the places of L.
V is a representation over Q_p, so det Ind V is Q_p^×-valued and SPM.3/conjugate-places-weights applies.
proofSteps: Put W = Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V; it is unramified outside a finite set and pure of weight n, since weights can be read on an open subgroup over which W is a sum of conjugates of V.

W|G_v ≅ ⊕_{w|v} Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} V|G_w (R01.1/mackey-decomposition) and D_dR,v(Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} V) ≅ D_dR,w(V) as filtered K_v-spaces (LV.1/de-rham-of-induced), so W is de Rham above p and gr^i D_dR,v(W) has K_v-dimension Σ_{w|v}[L_w : K_v] dim_{L_w} gr^i D_dR,w(V).
The character det W is Q_p^×-valued, pure of weight n·[L : K]·dim V, de Rham above p, with Hodge–Tate weight at v equal to Σ_i i·dim_{K_v} gr^i D_dR,v(W).
Apply SPM.3/conjugate-places-weights at the self-conjugate place v.
acceptance: For an abelian variety A over L = K of dimension g and V = H¹_ét(A_{K̄}, Q_p), both sides equal g at every self-conjugate v | p.

Applied to a subrepresentation W₀ with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} of a transitively induced symplectic module, it gives Σ_w [L_w : K_v] dim F¹D_dR,w(W₀) = ½ dim W₀ · #Σ, as used in the principal trichotomy.

sources.match: The sum over places w above a self-conjugate v of local degrees times Hodge–Tate weights of D_dR,w(V) is half the weight times [L : K] dim V, proved by applying Proposition 2.19 to the determinant of the induced representation.

nodes.title: Transport of D_pst on a spherical polyannulus
nodes.statement: Let K_v be a finite extension of Q_p, R_v = O_v⟨t₁^{±1}, …, t_n^{±1}⟩ and U = Sp(R_v[1/p]) the spherical polyannulus over K_v. Let (𝔼, E, c) be a de Rham pair on U (P8/associated-de-rham-pairs) whose filtered flat bundle E has a full basis of horizontal sections. Then for all y₀, y ∈ U(K_v) there is a unique isomorphism of (φ, N, G_v)-modules T_{y₀,y}: D_pst(𝔼_{ȳ₀}) → D_pst(𝔼_ȳ) such that, after extending scalars to K̄_v, it corresponds through c_BO and the fibre comparisons c_{y₀}: D_dR(𝔼_{ȳ₀}) ≅ E_{y₀} and c_y to 1 ⊗ T^∇_{y₀,y}: K̄_v ⊗ E_{y₀} → K̄_v ⊗ E_y.
hypotheses: U is a spherical polyannulus (inner and outer radii equal), so R_v satisfies Shimizu's Set-up 3.1 and Condition (BR).
E has a full basis of horizontal sections over U: (E, ∇) ≅ (O_U, d)^m.
proofSteps: Write E = H⁰(Ũ, 𝔼) for the G_{R_v}-representation of the local system (the polyannulus Galois-category equivalence, requested from P8), and choose lifts ỹ₀, ỹ of y₀, y, giving E_{ỹ₀} ≅ 𝔼_{ȳ₀} and E_ỹ ≅ 𝔼_ȳ.

A full horizontal basis makes E horizontal de Rham, and by Shimizu's relative monodromy theorem E becomes horizontal semistable over a finite extension: E is potentially horizontal semistable (P8/horizontal-and-local-system-monodromy; the extraction's E8 corrects the paper's citation to Shimizu Lemma 8.9 with Theorem 7.4).
By Shimizu's Lemma 4.4 (requested from P8) the specialisations ρ_ỹ: D^∇_pst(E) → D_pst(E_ỹ) are isomorphisms; put T_{y₀,y} := ρ_ỹ ∘ ρ_{ỹ₀}⁻¹.

Over B_dR(R_v) := H⁰(Ũ, OB_dR,U) there are G_{R_v}-equivariant isomorphisms with connection B_dR(R_v) ⊗ D^∇_pst(E) ≅ B_dR(R_v) ⊗ E ≅ B_dR(R_v) ⊗ E_U, the second the sections of c. Specialising along ỹ₀* gives the commuting diagram (∗∗) of the paper.

The rectangle (†) comparing these with 1 ⊗ ρ_{ỹ₀} and T^∇_{y₀} commutes up to an element of GL_n(K_v), because all its maps are G_{R_v}-equivariant horizontal isomorphisms and (B_dR(R_v))^{G_{R_v}, ∇=0} = K_v (the invariant base of P8/horizontal-relative-periods; Shimizu Proposition 4.9); it commutes after specialising at ỹ₀, by (∗∗), so it commutes. Specialising (†) along ỹ gives the claim.
Uniqueness: c_BO and the c_y are isomorphisms, so the K̄_v-extension of T_{y₀,y} is determined, hence T_{y₀,y} is.
acceptance: For a constant de Rham pair (𝔼 constant, E = O_U ⊗ D_dR) T_{y₀,y} is the identity of D_pst(𝔼_{ȳ₀}).
T_{y,y} = id and T_{y₁,y₂} ∘ T_{y₀,y₁} = T_{y₀,y₂}, by uniqueness.

sources.match: For a de Rham pair on a closed polydisc or spherical polyannulus whose bundle has a full basis of horizontal sections, there is a unique isomorphism of the D_pst of two fibres compatible with parallel transport through the comparison isomorphisms.

sources.locator: §3.5, Definition 3.24, Lemma 3.25, Corollary 3.26, Lemma 3.27, Remarks 3.28–3.29 and the proof of Theorem 3.22 for polyannuli, pp. 29–32

nodes.title: Reduction from closed polydiscs to spherical polyannuli
nodes.statement: If the conclusion of SPM.4/horizontal-transport-polyannulus holds for spherical polyannuli over every finite extension of Q_p, then it holds for every closed polydisc U over K_v, every de Rham pair on U whose bundle has a full basis of horizontal sections and every y₀, y ∈ U(K_v).
hypotheses: The residue field of K_v is arbitrary; the case k_v = F₂ needs the unramified extensions of degrees 2 and 3.
proofSteps: If k_v ≠ F₂: in coordinates y₀ = (a_i) and y = (b_i) with a_i, b_i ∈ O_v; choose c_i ∈ O_v outside the residue classes of a_i and b_i (possible since #k_v ≥ 3); t_i ↦ t_i − c_i embeds a spherical polyannulus U° ⊂ U containing y₀ and y; E|U° still has a full horizontal basis.

If k_v = F₂: for r = 2, 3 the unramified extension L_{w,r} has residue field with ≥ 4 elements, so the first case over L_{w,r} gives isomorphisms T_r of (φ, N, G_{w,r})-modules; by uniqueness T₂ = T₃ =: T. It commutes with G_{w,2} and G_{w,3}, which together generate G_v (their images in the unramified quotient Ẑ are 2Ẑ and 3Ẑ, and both contain inertia), so T is G_v-equivariant.
acceptance: Over Q₂ (residue field F₂) the argument passes through Q₄ and Q₈ = Q_{2³}, unramified of degrees 2 and 3.

sources.match: Theorem 3.22 for polydiscs reduces to polyannuli: embed a polyannulus through both points when the residue field is not F₂, and otherwise use unramified extensions of degrees 2 and 3, whose Galois groups generate G_v; uniqueness makes the isomorphisms agree.
The paragraph introducing the reduction says it begins the proof of Theorem 3.3; it begins the proof of Theorem 3.22 (this packet's E4).

nodes.title: Horizontal de Rham transport of D_pst
nodes.statement: Let U be a rigid-analytic space over a finite extension K_v of Q_p isomorphic to a closed polydisc or a spherical polyannulus, and (𝔼, E, c) a de Rham pair on U whose filtered flat bundle E has a full basis of horizontal sections. Then for all y₀, y ∈ U(K_v) there is a unique isomorphism of (φ, N, G_v)-modules T_{y₀,y}: D_pst(𝔼_{ȳ₀}) ≅ D_pst(𝔼_ȳ) whose K̄_v-extension corresponds, through c_BO and the fibre comparisons c_{y₀}, c_y, to 1 ⊗ T^∇_{y₀,y}. By uniqueness (a consequence not stated in the source), these isomorphisms satisfy T_{y,y} = id and T_{y₁,y₂} ∘ T_{y₀,y₁} = T_{y₀,y₂}, and are compatible with tensor products and morphisms of de Rham pairs.
hypotheses: U a closed polydisc or a spherical polyannulus over K_v; E with a full basis of horizontal sections on U.
proofSteps: For polyannuli this is SPM.4/horizontal-transport-polyannulus; for polydiscs apply SPM.4/polydisc-reduction.
The cocycle identity and the compatibilities follow from uniqueness, since parallel transport satisfies them.
acceptance: For the pushforward of the unit pair along a smooth proper family this is SPM.4/period-maps-control-dpst.

sources.match: The model-free comparison: on a polydisc or spherical polyannulus where the de Rham bundle has a full horizontal basis, the discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules of all fibres are canonically identified compatibly with parallel transport.
The same result appears in Betts, Local constancy of pro-unipotent Kummer maps, Theorem 6.1, which the paper re-derives from Shimizu.

nodes.title: Period maps control D_pst in smooth proper families
nodes.statement: Let π: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth varieties over a finite extension K_v of Q_p, i ≥ 0, and U ⊆ Y^an an admissible open isomorphic to a closed polydisc over which H^i_dR(X/Y)^an has a full basis of horizontal sections for the Gauss–Manin connection. Then for all y₀, y ∈ U(K_v) there is a unique isomorphism of (φ, N, G_v)-modules T_{y₀,y}: D_pst(H^i_ét(X_{y₀,K̄_v}, Q_p)) ≅ D_pst(H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)) whose K̄_v-extension corresponds, through c_BO and Scholze's comparison c_dR: D_dR(H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)) ≅ H^i_dR(X_y/K_v) at y₀ and at y, to 1 ⊗ T^∇_{y₀,y}: H^i_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v) → H^i_dR(X_y/K_v), the parallel transport composed with the base-change isomorphisms. In other words, H^i_pst(X_y/Q_p^nr) is constant on U(K_v) as a (φ, N, G_v)-module, and only the Hodge filtration moves.
hypotheses: No reduction hypothesis on π: K_v is any finite extension of Q_p, and π need not extend to any model.
c_dR is Scholze's comparison isomorphism, constructed from the relative comparison (P8); the statement is for that c_dR (Betts–Stix Remark 3.4).
proofSteps: Apply the relative comparison to π^an and the unit de Rham pair (Ẑ_p, O_{X^an}, 1): (R^iπ^an_*Ẑ_p, R^iπ^an_dR,*O, c_dR) is a de Rham pair on Y^an (P8/de-rham-pair-derived-pushforward).

By the analytification comparisons (P8/de-rham-pair-pushforward-compatibilities) these are the analytifications of R^iπ_ét,*Z_p and of H^i_dR(X/Y) with its Gauss–Manin connection (ComplexComparisonPartII C5/gauss-manin-connection), and the fibre of c_dR at a K_v-point is Scholze's c_dR for the fibre (Betts–Stix (3.8)).
Apply SPM.4/horizontal-de-rham-transport to the restriction of this pair to U.
acceptance: For π with good reduction on a residue disk, Lawrence–Venkatesh obtain an analogous transport through crystalline cohomology (LV.4/fibre-filtered-phi-transport); identifying the two needs a comparison of Scholze's c_dR with the crystalline comparison, which Betts–Stix (Remark 3.4) note is not covered by Nizioł's comparison results, so this roadmap does not use it.
The isomorphism class of H^i_pH(X_y/K_v) is not constant on U in general; only its (φ, N, G_v)-module is.

sources.match: For a smooth proper family and a polydisc on which relative de Rham cohomology has a full horizontal basis, the D_pst of the étale cohomology of fibres are identified compatibly with parallel transport; the comparison isomorphism used is Scholze's.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 3.3 from Theorem 3.22, p. 29
sources.match: Apply Scholze's relative comparison to the unit pair to get a de Rham pair whose components are the analytified relative étale and de Rham cohomology, and use Theorem 3.22.
The presentation avoids good reduction and models, replacing crystalline cohomology by relative p-adic Hodge theory of Scholze and Shimizu.

nodes.title: Period maps control the local Galois representations
nodes.statement: Let π: X → Y, i and U ∋ y₀ be as in SPM.4/period-maps-control-dpst, and Φ_{y₀}: U → G^an_{y₀} the v-adic period map of the filtered flat bundle H^i_dR(X/Y)^an (requested from LV.3 in the model-free form), G_{y₀} the flag variety of filtrations of H^i_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v) with the dimension data of its Hodge filtration. For a filtration Φ ∈ G_{y₀}(K_v) let M^i(Φ) := (H^i_pst(X_{y₀}/Q_p^nr), H^i_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v) filtered by Φ, c_dR ∘ c_BO), the retwist of SPM.2/automorphism-group. Then H^i_pH(X_y/K_v) ≅ M^i(Φ_{y₀}(y)) as filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules for every y ∈ U(K_v). Hence, D_pH being fully faithful, Φ_{y₀}(y) determines the isomorphism class of the G_v-representation H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p), and two points y, y′ ∈ U(K_v) with Φ_{y₀}(y), Φ_{y₀}(y′) in one Aut(H^i_pst(X_{y₀}))(Q_p)-orbit have isomorphic local representations.
hypotheses: As in SPM.4/period-maps-control-dpst; the filtration of the bundle is the Hodge filtration, which is Griffiths transverse, though Definition 3.1 does not need this.
proofSteps: The isomorphism T_{y₀,y} of SPM.4/period-maps-control-dpst, paired with T^∇_{y₀,y} on de Rham cohomology, is an isomorphism M^i(Φ_{y₀}(y)) → H^i_pH(X_y/K_v): by definition of Φ_{y₀}, T^∇_{y₀,y} carries the filtration Φ_{y₀}(y) to the Hodge filtration of X_y.
Full faithfulness of D_pH (requested from R06.3) turns an isomorphism of p-adic Hodge cohomology into an isomorphism of representations.
The orbit statement is SPM.2/orbit-lemma.
acceptance: At y = y₀, Φ_{y₀}(y₀) is the Hodge filtration and M^i(Φ_{y₀}(y₀)) = H^i_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v).
In diagram form: the map y ↦ [H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v})] from U(K_v) to isomorphism classes of de Rham G_v-representations factors through Φ_{y₀}, M^i and D_pH.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.5 and the diagram after it, pp. 17–18
sources.match: For y in the polydisc, the p-adic Hodge cohomology of the fibre at y is the base-point module with its filtration replaced by the period map value; since D_pH is fully faithful, the period map determines the isomorphism class of the local representation.

nodes.title: The symplectic pair of p-adic Hodge cohomology of a fibre
nodes.statement: Let X → Y′ → Y be an abelian-by-finite family over a scheme Y of characteristic zero with polarisation λ, K_v a finite extension of Q_p and y ∈ Y(K_v). Then Scholze's comparison c_dR identifies the étale and de Rham first Chern classes of λ, c₁^ét(λ) ↔ c₁^dR(λ), so that the étale pairing ω_λ^ét and the de Rham pairing ω_λ^dR correspond, and H^{≤1}_pH(X_y/K_v) := (H⁰_pH(X_y/K_v), H¹_pH(X_y/K_v)) with pairing ω_λ^pH: ∧²H¹_pH → H⁰_pH⟨−1⟩ (components D_pst(ω_λ^ét) and ω_λ^dR) is a symplectic pair in MF(φ, N, G_v). It is isomorphic to D_pH(H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)) as a symplectic pair.
hypotheses: ⟨−1⟩ is the Tate twist of filtered modules, D_dR shifted so that its filtration jump moves by one; the identification of Q_p(−1) with ⟨−1⟩ uses the isomorphism a: B_dR(−1) ≅ B_dR⟨−1⟩ of CohomologyComparisons CP.6/trace-normalized-tate-period.
proofSteps: c_dR is an isomorphism of graded algebras, natural and compatible with base change (CP.6/naturality-base-change-and-cup-products), so H⁰_pH is an algebra and H¹_pH a module over it in MF(φ, N, G_v).

c_dR ⊗ a⁻¹ carries c₁^ét of the line bundle (1, λ)^*P to c₁^dR (CP.6/first-chern-class-comparison; the paper's argument through the total space of the line bundle is repaired as in the extraction's E3).
Hence the étale and de Rham pairings, each perfect by the model-free Lemmas 4.2 and 4.6 requested from LV.2, match under the comparison, and ω_λ^pH is a perfect pairing in MF(φ, N, G_v).
The comparison with D_pH of the étale pair is the definition of H^•_pH (SPM.2/restriction-induction).
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over K_v, H^{≤1}_pH(E/K_v) is (1, H¹_pH(E)) with the pairing into 1⟨−1⟩ given by D_pst of the Weil pairing and the de Rham cup product.

sources.match: Over K_v, Scholze's comparison identifies the étale and de Rham Chern classes of the polarisation, so the two pairings correspond and the p-adic Hodge cohomology of a fibre in degrees ≤ 1 is a symplectic pair of filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules.
Compatibility of c_dR with traces, duality, cycle and Chern classes through the isomorphism a.

nodes.title: The symplectic pairs M^{≤1}(Φ) of Lagrangian filtrations
nodes.statement: Let X → Y′ → Y be an abelian-by-finite family over a smooth K_v-variety Y and y₀ ∈ Y(K_v). Let H_{y₀} be the K_v-variety of Lagrangian H⁰_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v)-submodules of H¹_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v) (the period variety LV.3/lagrangian-period-variety of the symplectic module H¹_dR over the finite étale algebra H⁰_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v) = O(Y′_{y₀})), a closed subvariety of the flag variety G_{y₀}. For Φ ∈ H_{y₀}(K_v), M¹(Φ) := (H¹_pst(X_{y₀}/Q_p^nr), H¹_dR(X_{y₀}/K_v), c_dR ∘ c_BO) with the filtration F^i = H¹_dR for i ≤ 0, F¹ = Φ, F^i = 0 for i ≥ 2, and M⁰ := H⁰_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v). Then M¹(Φ) is a symplectic M⁰-module in MF(φ, N, G_v) for the pairing ω_λ^pH, and M^{≤1}(Φ) := (M⁰, M¹(Φ)) is a symplectic pair. The Hodge filtration point Φ₀ = F¹H¹_dR(X_{y₀}) gives M^{≤1}(Φ₀) = H^{≤1}_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v).
hypotheses: Φ is Lagrangian for ω_λ^dR, which is what makes the retwisted pairing a morphism of filtered modules into M⁰⟨−1⟩.
proofSteps: M¹(Φ) is the retwist of SPM.2/automorphism-group of H¹_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v) by the two-step filtration Φ.

The pairing ω_λ^pH: ∧² M¹(Φ) → M⁰⟨−1⟩ respects filtrations exactly when ω_λ^dR(Φ, Φ) = 0, i.e. Φ isotropic, and it is perfect as a filtered pairing exactly when Φ is Lagrangian (rank d over H⁰_dR on each factor).
The algebra M⁰ is untouched, and at Φ₀ the retwist is the identity.
acceptance: At Φ₀ one recovers H^{≤1}_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v) (SPM.5/p-adic-hodge-symplectic-pair).
For an elliptic curve (d = 1, Y′ = Y) H_{y₀} = P¹ and M¹(Φ) is H¹_pst(E_{y₀}) with F¹ the line Φ.

sources.match: The Lagrangian period domain H_{y₀} and, for each Lagrangian Φ, the symplectic pair M^{≤1}(Φ) obtained from the p-adic Hodge cohomology of the base fibre by replacing the Hodge filtration of H¹_dR with the two-step filtration given by Φ.

nodes.title: Period maps of abelian-by-finite families
nodes.statement: Let X → Y′ → Y be an abelian-by-finite family over a smooth variety Y over a finite extension K_v of Q_p, y₀ ∈ Y(K_v), and U_{y₀} ⊆ Y^an an admissible open isomorphic to a closed polydisc over which H⁰_dR(X/Y)^an and H¹_dR(X/Y)^an have full bases of horizontal sections. Then the period map Φ_{y₀} of H¹_dR(X/Y) takes values in H^an_{y₀}, and for every y ∈ U_{y₀}(K_v), D_pH(H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)) ≅ H^{≤1}_pH(X_y/K_v) ≅ M^{≤1}(Φ_{y₀}(y)) as symplectic pairs in MF(φ, N, G_v). That is, the map Y(K_v) → π₀SP(Rep^dR_{Q_p}(G_v)), y ↦ [H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)], restricted to U_{y₀}(K_v), equals the composite of Φ_{y₀}, M^{≤1} and the inverse of D_pH on isomorphism classes (D_pH is injective on isomorphism classes by full faithfulness, and M^{≤1}(Φ_{y₀}(y)) lies in its image).
hypotheses: No model or reduction hypothesis; K_v any finite extension of Q_p.
proofSteps: Parallel transport on H⁰_dR and H¹_dR respects the algebra, module and pairing structures (model-free Lemma 4.8 requested from LV.2), so Φ_{y₀}(y) is a Lagrangian submodule and Φ_{y₀} lands in H^an_{y₀}.

The first isomorphism is SPM.5/p-adic-hodge-symplectic-pair; the second is SPM.4/period-map-controls-local-representations for i = 0, 1, the transport isomorphisms T_{y₀,y} being compatible with products and the pairing because they are unique (SPM.4/horizontal-de-rham-transport).
On H⁰ the period map is constant, since H⁰_dR has trivial filtration; so the algebra is M⁰ throughout.
acceptance: Consequently two points of U_{y₀}(K_v) with the same period value have isomorphic symplectic pairs of local representations.

Parallel transport respects the algebra, module and pairing structures, so the period map of an abelian-by-finite family lands in the Lagrangian period domain.

nodes.statement: In the setting of SPM.5/lagrangian-period-modules, let (y′_i)_{i∈I} be the closed points of Y′_{y₀}, L_{w_i} := K_v(y′_i) with a fixed K_v-embedding into K̄_v and G_{w_i} ≤ G_v. Then H_{y₀} = ∏_i Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i} with H_{y′_i} := LGrass(H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i})) (4.3); every Φ ∈ H_{y₀}(K_v) is a product ∏_i Φ′_i of Lagrangian L_{w_i}-subspaces Φ′_i of H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}); and M¹(Φ) = ∏_i Ind_{G_{w_i}}^{G_v} M¹_i(Φ′_i) in MF(φ, N, G_v), compatibly with the symplectic structures over M⁰ ≅ ∏_i Ind_{G_{w_i}}^{G_v} 1, where M¹_i(Φ′_i) := (H¹_pst(X_{y′_i}/Q_p^nr), H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}) with F¹ = Φ′_i, c_dR ∘ c_BO) in MF(φ, N, G_{w_i}).
hypotheses: The printed lemma writes H¹_dR(X_{y′_0}/L_{w_i}) for the i-th factor and indexes the product (4.3) by y′_0; the correct indices are y′_i (extraction E4 and this packet's E6).
proofSteps: The decomposition X_{y₀} = ⊔_i X_{y′_i} gives H¹_pH(X_{y₀}/K_v) = ∏_i Ind_{G_{w_i}}^{G_v} H¹_pH(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}) by (2.2) of SPM.2/restriction-induction, compatibly with the module structure over H⁰_pH = ∏ Ind 1.

A Lagrangian H⁰_dR = ∏_i L_{w_i}-submodule of ∏_i H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}) is a product of Lagrangian L_{w_i}-subspaces; this is the factorisation of LV.3/lagrangian-period-variety-splitting, written with Weil restriction (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).
Replacing the Hodge filtrations by Φ and the Φ′_i respects the decomposition.
acceptance: dim_{K_v} H_{y₀} = Σ_i [L_{w_i} : K_v]·d(d + 1)/2, where d is the constant relative dimension.

sources.match: The period domain is the product over the closed points of Y′_{y₀} of Weil restrictions of Lagrangian Grassmannians, and M¹(Φ) is the product of the inductions of the factor modules, compatibly with the symplectic structure over M⁰.

nodes.title: S-good symplectic pairs
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, S a finite set of places of K and p a prime. A symplectic pair (A, V) of continuous Q_p-representations of G_K (SPM.1/symplectic-pair) is S-good when: (i) A is unramified outside S; (ii) V is unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside S (R34.1/pure-and-integral-galois-representations); (iii) V is de Rham at every place above p with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1}. It is Artin S-good if moreover A has finite image (A pure and integral of weight 0).
hypotheses: S is arbitrary in the definition; in the loci below it contains the places above p∞ and the places of bad reduction of the family ('suitable').
Weights are those of geometric Frobenius (q_u-Weil numbers); Hodge–Tate weights are normalised so that Q_p(1) has weight −1.
proofSteps: Each condition is a condition on the restrictions to decomposition groups (R01.2/local-restriction), independent of the chosen embeddings.
All three conditions pass to isomorphic pairs, so S-goodness is a property of isomorphism classes.
acceptance: The pair of a fibre H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p) at y ∈ Y(K) is S-good for suitable S (SPM.6/rational-points-in-lv-locus).
S-good pairs with A = Q_p and V GSp-irreducible of rank 2d fall into finitely many isomorphism classes (the symplectic Faltings lemma requested from LV.1).

sources.match: A pair of an algebra and a symplectic module in Galois representations is S-good when the algebra is unramified outside S, the module unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside S, and de Rham above p with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1.
Requiring the algebra to be an Artin representation changes none of the loci, since an interpolating algebra is split and has finite automorphism group.

nodes.title: The Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, X → Y′ → Y an abelian-by-finite family, p a prime, v a place of K above p and S a finite set of places containing the places above p∞ and the places of bad reduction of the family (a place u is of good reduction when the family extends to an abelian-by-finite family over a smooth proper model of Y over O_u). The Lawrence–Venkatesh locus Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} ⊆ Y(K_v) is the set of y_v for which some S-good pair (A, V) (SPM.6/s-good-pair) satisfies H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) ≅ (A|G_v, V|G_v) as symplectic pairs of G_v-representations; (A, V) interpolates y_v. Requiring (A, V) Artin S-good gives the same set.
hypotheses: S suitable: containing the places above p and ∞ and those of bad reduction; enlarging S enlarges the locus.
Only the single place v is interpolated, unlike the adelic locus of SPM.1/adelic-lv-locus.
proofSteps: The condition compares symplectic pairs of G_v-representations; it depends on (A, V) only up to isomorphism.

Remark 6.3: if (A, V) interpolates y_v then A|G_v ≅ H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}) is split (SPM.6/fibre-algebra-points), so A ≅ Q_p^n as an algebra and its automorphism group is finite; the G_K-action on A therefore has finite image and A is Artin.
acceptance: Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} (SPM.6/rational-points-in-lv-locus).
For the constant family Y × A₀ the locus is all of Y(K_v).

sources.locator: Definition 1.2, p. 2, and Definition 6.2 with footnotes 20–21, pp. 43–44
sources.match: For a suitable S, the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus is the set of local points whose fibre cohomology in degrees ≤ 1, as a symplectic pair of local representations, is the restriction of an S-good global pair; good reduction means the family extends over a smooth proper model.
Adding the Artin condition does not change the locus.

nodes.title: The Lawrence–Venkatesh locus in the period domain
nodes.statement: In the setting of SPM.6/lawrence-venkatesh-locus, let y₀ ∈ Y(K_v) and H_{y₀} the Lagrangian period domain (SPM.5/lagrangian-period-modules). Then H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S} ⊆ H_{y₀}(K_v) is the set of Lagrangians Φ for which some S-good pair (A, V) satisfies M^{≤1}(Φ) ≅ (D_pH(A|G_v), D_pH(V|G_v)) as symplectic pairs in MF(φ, N, G_v). For a closed polydisc U_{y₀} ∋ y₀ as in SPM.5/abelian-by-finite-period-diagram, Φ_{y₀}(U_{y₀}(K_v) ∩ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S}) ⊆ H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S}. Consequently Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is finite as soon as, for every y₀ ∈ Y(K_v), (i) Φ_{y₀} has Zariski-dense image in H_{y₀} and (ii) H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is not Zariski dense in H_{y₀}.
hypotheses: Y is a smooth projective curve, so Y(K_v) is compact and covered by finitely many discs U_{y₀}(K_v) (the properness needed by Remark 5.11, this packet's E3).
proofSteps: The inclusion is SPM.5/abelian-by-finite-period-diagram: D_pH of the fibre pair at y is M^{≤1}(Φ_{y₀}(y)), and D_pH of an interpolating pair is (D_pH(A|G_v), D_pH(V|G_v)).

If (i) and (ii) hold, U_{y₀}(K_v) ∩ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} lies in the preimage of a proper Zariski-closed subset, which in a disc is the zero set of a non-zero coherent ideal, hence finite (the model-free Corollary 5.10 requested from LV.3).
Cover the compact Y(K_v) by finitely many such discs.
acceptance: Condition (i) holds under full monodromy (model-free Lemma 5.9, requested from LV.3); (ii) is proved type by type in SPM.7 and SPM.8.

sources.locator: Definition 1.7 and the paragraph after it, §1.1.2, p. 5
sources.match: The period-domain locus is the set of Lagrangians whose retwisted symplectic pair matches D_pH of an S-good pair; the period map sends the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus into it, so density of the period map and non-density of this set give finiteness.
Finiteness of the whole locus follows from finiteness on each disc by compactness of Y(K_v).
