nodes.title: Interpolating pairs are S-good
nodes.statement: Let X → Y′ → Y, p and S be as in SPM.6/lawrence-venkatesh-locus (S suitable). If (A, V) interpolates an adelic point (y_u)_u ∈ Y(A_K)^LV_X (SPM.1/adelic-lv-locus), then (A, V) is S-good. Hence Y(K_v)^LV_X ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} for every p-adic place v.
hypotheses: S suitable; (A, V) interpolates at every place, which is what gives the global conditions.
proofSteps: At u ∉ S, y_u ∈ Y(K_u) extends to an O_u-point of the smooth proper model (properness), over which the family extends; so Y′_{y_u} is finite étale over O_u and H⁰_ét(X_{y_u}) ≅ A|G_u is unramified.

At u ∉ S, each X_{y′} over K_u(y′) has good reduction, so H¹_ét(X_{y_u}) ≅ V|G_u is unramified with integral Frobenius polynomial whose roots are q_u-Weil numbers of weight 1 (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.6/good-reduction-frobenius-polynomial; LV.1/abelian-variety-cohomology-properties).
At u | p, H¹_ét of each abelian fibre is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} (R06.5/proper-smooth-rational-de-rham-comparison), so V|G_u is.
Projecting to v gives the inclusion.
acceptance: For the diagonal image of y ∈ Y(K) this gives the S-goodness of H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p).

sources.match: An adelic point of the adelic locus is interpolated by an S-good pair for any S containing the places above p∞ and of bad reduction, because the local fibre representations are unramified, pure and integral at good places and de Rham with weights 0 and 1 above p.

nodes.title: Rational points lie in the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
nodes.statement: For every abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y over a smooth projective geometrically connected curve Y/K, every prime p, every place v | p and every suitable S, the image of Y(K) in Y(K_v) lies in Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S}; each y ∈ Y(K) is interpolated by H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p) with its G_K-action.
hypotheses: S suitable for the family.
proofSteps: The diagonal point of y lies in Y(A_K)^LV_X, interpolated by H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p) (SPM.1/adelic-lv-locus); apply SPM.6/adelic-locus-in-lv-locus.
acceptance: This is the 'almost tautological' half of the Lawrence–Venkatesh method in obstruction form ((1°) of Betts–Stix Remark 1.3).

sources.match: Rational points lie in the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus of every abelian-by-finite family, interpolated by the cohomology of their own fibre, which is S-good by Lemma 6.4; so Theorem 6.5 reproves the Mordell conjecture.

nodes.title: The non-symplectic Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
nodes.statement: In the setting of SPM.6/lawrence-venkatesh-locus, Y(K_v)^{LV°}_{X,S} is defined in the same way with 'symplectic' omitted throughout: pairs (A, V) of a commutative algebra and a finite locally free A-module in Q_p-representations of G_K satisfying the conditions of SPM.6/s-good-pair, and isomorphisms of algebra–module pairs H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}) ≅ (A|G_v, V|G_v). Then Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} ⊆ Y(K_v)^{LV°}_{X,S}. For the Kodaira–Parshin family X_q of a curve of genus g, the relative dimension is d_q = (g − 1/2)(q − 1); for a curve of genus 3 over Q the Lawrence–Venkatesh argument for Y(K_v)^{LV°} needs q ≥ 23 (d_q ≥ 55), while the symplectic argument of this roadmap works with q = 11 (d_q = 25) at a place where q = 11 satisfies the conditions of SPM.8/parameter-comparison (with the good-reduction form of its condition (3)).
hypotheses: The comparison of the two values of q uses the conditions of SPM.8/parameter-comparison (Remark 6.23(III)), the value q = 11 with n_v replaced by 2 at a place of good reduction.
proofSteps: Forgetting the pairing maps S-good pairs to S-good algebra–module pairs and isomorphisms of symplectic pairs to isomorphisms of algebra–module pairs, which gives the inclusion.
acceptance: For a polarised family of elliptic curves (Y′ = Y, d = 1) the two loci coincide (an observation not made in the source): A = Q_p, and a rank-two V is a symplectic module with L := ∧²V and ω the identity, any symplectic structure on V being isomorphic to this one through ω; an isomorphism f_V of modules then gives an isomorphism of pairs with f_L = ∧²f_V.

sources.match: Lawrence and Venkatesh constrain the larger locus without the symplectic condition; the symplectic formulation needs smaller families, e.g. q = 11 (relative dimension 25) instead of q ≥ 23 (relative dimension 55) for a genus-3 curve over Q.
The smallest q satisfying the original conditions is 23 and the smallest for this paper's conditions is 11, for genus 3.

nodes.title: The algebra of a fibre and its points
nodes.statement: For an abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y and y_v ∈ Y(K_v), H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) = H⁰_ét(Y′_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) = ∏_{Y′_{y_v}(K̄_v)} Q_p is a split Q_p-algebra, and there is a canonical G_v-equivariant bijection between its Q_p-algebra maps ψ to Q_p and Y′_{y_v}(K̄_v). Such a ψ is a closed point y′_v of Y′_{y_v} with a K_v-embedding K_v(y′_v) → K̄_v; its stabiliser G_{w_ψ} is the Galois group of K_v(y′_v), so [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] = [K_v(y′_v) : K_v], and #Σ = dim_{Q_p} H⁰_ét.
hypotheses: Σ is the set of Q_p-points of the algebra; here the algebra is split, so #Σ equals its dimension, which fails for a non-split algebra such as Q_{p²} (extraction E1).
proofSteps: X_{y_v} → Y′_{y_v} has geometrically connected fibres (abelian varieties), so H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}) = H⁰_ét(Y′_{y_v,K̄_v}) = functions on the finite set Y′_{y_v}(K̄_v).
Algebra maps from a product of copies of Q_p to Q_p are the projections; the G_v-action on the index set is the Galois action on geometric points.
The stabiliser of a geometric point over a closed point y′ is the absolute Galois group of its residue field.
acceptance: If Y′_{y_v} is a single point with residue field of degree 4 over K_v, Σ is one G_v-orbit of size 4.

sources.match: H⁰ of the fibre is the product of copies of Q_p indexed by the geometric points of Y′_{y_v}, so algebra maps to Q_p are those points, and the index condition [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 means the residue field has degree at least 4.

nodes.title: The principal trichotomy
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, v a self-conjugate place above p (SPM.3/self-conjugate-place) and (A, V) a symplectic pair of continuous Q_p-representations of G_K with V of rank 2d > 0 over A, de Rham at the places above p, with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} at v, and unramified and pure of weight 1 outside a finite set. Let Σ = Σ_A = Hom_{Q_p-alg}(A, Q_p), and for ψ ∈ Σ let G_ψ ≤ G_K be its stabiliser, G_{w_ψ} = G_ψ ∩ G_v, and V_ψ = Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V. Then at least one of the following holds: (a) some ψ ∈ Σ has [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and V_ψ is GSp-irreducible as a symplectic representation of G_ψ; (b) some ψ ∈ Σ has [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and V_ψ has a non-zero isotropic G_ψ-subrepresentation W with dim F¹D_dR,w_ψ(W) ≥ ½ dim_{Q_p} W (average Hodge–Tate weight ≥ 1/2 at w_ψ); (c) the number of ψ ∈ Σ with [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4 is at least #Σ/(d + 1). When A is split (A ≅ Q_p^n as a Q_p-algebra, as for every algebra H⁰_ét of a fibre), #Σ = dim_{Q_p}(A) and (c) reads #{ψ : [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4} ≥ dim_{Q_p}(A)/(d + 1).
hypotheses: v self-conjugate. Σ consists of the Q_p-points of A; with dim_{Q_p}(A) in place of #Σ, (c) is false for non-reduced or non-split A (extraction E1: A = Q_p[ε]/(ε³) or A = Q_{p²} with an elliptic curve give counterexamples).
GSp-irreducible is in the sense of the LV.1 request (no non-zero stable isotropic subspace).
proofSteps: Reduction: split Σ into G_K-orbits Σ_i and put A_i = ∏_{ψ∈Σ_i} Q_p, V_i = A_i ⊗_A V. (A, V) satisfies (a) or (b) iff some (A_i, V_i) does, and if every (A_i, V_i) satisfies (c) then so does (A, V), summing over orbits.

For one orbit with base point ψ₀ and L = L_{ψ₀}, V_i ≅ Ind_{G_{ψ₀}}^{G_K} V_{ψ₀} over A_i = Ind Q_p (SPM.1/symplectic-pair). Suppose (a) and (b) fail; if no G_v-orbit in Σ_i has size ≥ 4, (c) holds; otherwise take ψ₀ with [G_v : G_{w_{ψ₀}}] ≥ 4.

Failure of (a) gives a non-zero isotropic G_{ψ₀}-stable W₀ ≤ V_{ψ₀}; its conjugates σ⁻¹(W₀) ≤ V_{ψ₀·σ} are isotropic, de Rham with weights in {0, 1}, and failure of (b) gives dim F¹D_dR(σ⁻¹W₀) ≤ ½(dim W₀ − 1) whenever ψ₀·σ lies in a G_v-orbit of size ≥ 4.

Summing over coset representatives (each place w of L above v occurring [L_w : K_v] times) and using the trivial bound dim F¹ ≤ dim W₀ on the small orbits: Σ_w [L_w : K_v] dim F¹D_dR,w(W₀) ≤ ½(dim W₀ − 1)(#Σ_i − #Σ_{i,<4}) + dim W₀ · #Σ_{i,<4}.

SPM.3/average-hodge-tate-weight gives the left side = ½ dim W₀ · #Σ_i. Rearranging, (dim W₀ + 1)·#Σ_{i,<4} ≥ #Σ_i, and dim W₀ ≤ d (isotropic in a 2d-dimensional symplectic space), which is (c) for the orbit.
acceptance: For A = Q_p (Σ a single point fixed by G_v), (c) holds since 1 ≥ 1/(d + 1): the trichotomy says nothing for polarised abelian schemes, which is why the abelian-by-finite structure is needed.
The Lawrence–Venkatesh division of points (their Lemmas 6.1, 6.2 and the proof of Theorem 5.4) corresponds roughly to types (b), (a) and (c) (Betts–Stix Remark 1.9).

sources.locator: Proposition 6.7 and proof, pp. 46–47; Proposition 1.8 and Remark 1.9, pp. 5–6
sources.match: At a self-conjugate place, every pair of an algebra and a symplectic module of the stated kind is of one of three types: an index-≥4 point with GSp-irreducible fibre, an index-≥4 point with an isotropic subrepresentation of average Hodge–Tate weight at least one half, or many points with small orbits; the proof combines the orbit decomposition with Corollary 2.21.
Σ_A is the set of Q_p-algebra maps A → Q_p; the reduction to split transitive algebras.

nodes.title: Types (a), (b), (c) and their loci
nodes.statement: Let S be a finite set of places, p a prime and v a place above p. (a) An S-good pair (A, V) of G_K-representations is of type (a) if some ψ ∈ Σ_A has [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and V_ψ is GSp-irreducible as a symplectic representation of G_ψ. (b) A symplectic pair (A, V) of G_v-representations is of type (b) if some ψ ∈ Σ_A has [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and V_ψ has a non-zero isotropic G_{w_ψ}-subrepresentation of average Hodge–Tate weight ≥ 1/2. (c) For d > 0, an algebra A in G_v-representations is of type (c) if #{ψ ∈ Σ_A : [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4} ≥ dim_{Q_p}(A)/(d + 1). For an abelian-by-finite family of constant relative dimension d > 0 and suitable S: Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} is the set of y_v interpolated by an S-good pair of type (a); Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} the set of y_v with H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}) of type (b); Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(c)} the set of y_v with H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}) of type (c). If v is self-conjugate, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} ∪ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} ∪ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(c)}.
hypotheses: Type (c) is stated with dim_{Q_p}(A), as printed; it is evaluated only on algebras H⁰_ét of fibres, which are split, where it agrees with the corrected trichotomy (extraction E1).
Type (b) is local: a global G_ψ-subrepresentation as in the trichotomy restricts to a G_{w_ψ}-subrepresentation.
proofSteps: Each type is invariant under isomorphism of pairs (respectively of algebras) and is local at v except (a).

Containment: if (A, V) interpolates y_v, then A ≅ H⁰_ét(X_{y_v}) as algebras is split (SPM.6/fibre-algebra-points), so the trichotomy (SPM.6/principal-trichotomy) applies with #Σ = dim A. Its case (a) is type (a); its case (b) gives, by restriction and transport through the interpolating isomorphism, type (b) for H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v}); its case (c) is type (c) for H⁰_ét(X_{y_v}) ≅ A|G_v.
acceptance: Points of type (a) are handled by Faltings' lemma and dimension counts, type (b) by the general-position lemma, and type (c) by choosing the family (SPM.7, SPM.8).

nodes.title: The finite sets T_i of local classes of type (a)
nodes.statement: In the setting of SPM.5/period-domain-decomposition, with S suitable, let d_i := dim X_{y′_i} (the relative dimension) and δ := deg(Y′ → Y). T_i is the set of isomorphism classes of symplectic modules D of rank 2d_i over the unit object 1 of MF(φ, N, G_{w_i}) for which there exist: a finite extension L/K of degree ≤ δ, unramified outside S; a v-adic place w_i of L with L_{w_i} ≅ K_v(y′_i) over K_v; and a GSp-irreducible symplectic representation V of G_L, de Rham at the places above p and unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside the places above S; with D ≅ D_pH,w_i(V|G_{w_i}) as symplectic filtered discrete (φ, N, G_{w_i})-modules. H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a) ⊆ H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i}) is the set of Lagrangians Φ′_i with [M¹_i(Φ′_i)] ∈ T_i.
hypotheses: S suitable; L ranges over extensions of degree at most δ inside a fixed algebraic closure.
proofSteps: T_i is the image of a set of (L, w_i, V) under D_pH,w_i; finiteness is SPM.7/type-a-classes-finite.
acceptance: If [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a) is not Zariski dense in Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i} (SPM.7/type-a-factor-non-density).

nodes.title: Finiteness of the sets T_i
nodes.statement: Each set T_i of SPM.7/type-a-classes is finite.
hypotheses: S finite; δ fixed.
proofSteps: By Hermite–Minkowski there are finitely many L/K of degree ≤ δ unramified outside S (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3/hermite-unramified-outside-finite).

For each L, the symplectic Faltings lemma (requested from LV.1) gives finitely many isomorphism classes of GSp-irreducible symplectic representations of G_L of rank 2d_i, unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside S.
Each L has finitely many places w_i; each triple gives one class D_pH,w_i(V|G_{w_i}).
acceptance: GSp-irreducibility is what lets Faltings's finiteness apply: LV.1/faltings-finiteness counts semisimple representations only, and nothing bounds the non-semisimple S-good pairs, which is why types (b) and (c) are handled differently.

sources.match: T_i is finite, by Hermite–Minkowski and the symplectic Faltings lemma.

nodes.title: Non-density of type (a) Lagrangians after Weil restriction
nodes.statement: If [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, then H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a) is not Zariski dense in Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}. It may be dense in H_{y′_i} itself; the Weil restriction to K_v is essential.
hypotheses: [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4 and d_i ≥ 1.
proofSteps: By SPM.7/type-a-classes-finite and SPM.2/orbit-lemma, H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a) is a finite union of orbits of Aut^GSp(H¹_pst(X_{y′_i}/Q_p^nr))(Q_p), which acts Q_p-algebraically on Res^{L_{w_i}}_{Q_p} H_{y′_i}.
The scalars act trivially, so by SPM.2/automorphism-dimension-bound the orbits lie in a closed Q_p-subvariety of dimension ≤ d_i(2d_i + 1).
By the adjunction between base change and Weil restriction, the set then lies in a closed K_v-subvariety of Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i} of K_v-dimension ≤ d_i(2d_i + 1).
dim_{K_v} Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i} = [L_{w_i} : K_v]·d_i(d_i + 1)/2 ≥ 2d_i² + 2d_i > d_i(2d_i + 1) (LV.3/lagrangian-grassmannian-geometry gives dim H_{y′_i} = d_i(d_i + 1)/2).
acceptance: For d_i = 1 and [L_{w_i} : K_v] = 4: the orbits have dimension ≤ 3 while Res H_{y′_i} = Res P¹ has dimension 4.
For [L_{w_i} : K_v] = 3 and d_i = 1 the count 3 ≤ 3 gives nothing, which is why index ≥ 4 appears.

sources.match: For residue degree at least 4, the Lagrangians with type (a) class are not Zariski dense in the Weil restriction of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, by finiteness of T_i, the orbit lemma and the dimension bound d(2d + 1) against [L : K_v]·d(d + 1)/2.

nodes.title: Non-density of the type (a) period locus
nodes.statement: For y₀ ∈ Y(K_v), let H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} be the set of Lagrangians Φ ∈ H_{y₀}(K_v) for which some S-good pair (A, V) of type (a) satisfies M^{≤1}(Φ) ≅ (D_pH(A|G_v), D_pH(V|G_v)) as symplectic pairs in MF(φ, N, G_v). Then H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} is not Zariski dense in H_{y₀}.
hypotheses: S suitable; any abelian-by-finite family (no monodromy hypothesis here).
proofSteps: Given Φ in the set with its pair (A, V) and point ψ of type (a): the algebra part of the isomorphism is D_pH of an isomorphism H⁰_ét(X_{y₀}) ≅ A|G_v (full faithfulness, requested from R06.3), so ψ corresponds to a geometric K̄_v-point of Y′_{y₀}, i.e. a closed point y′_i together with a K_v-embedding of its residue field into K̄_v; after moving ψ in its G_v-orbit, the fixed embedding of L_{w_i}.

Then [L_{w_i} : K_v] = [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and D_pH,w_ψ(V_ψ|G_{w_ψ}) ≅ M¹_i(Φ′_i) by SPM.5/period-domain-decomposition, and (L_ψ, w_ψ, V_ψ) witnesses [M¹_i(Φ′_i)] ∈ T_i; so Φ′_i ∈ H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a).
So the set lies in ⋃_{i: [L_{w_i}:K_v] ≥ 4} (pr_i)⁻¹(closure of H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a)), a finite union of proper closed subsets by SPM.7/type-a-factor-non-density and the product decomposition (4.3).
acceptance: If every closed point of Y′_{y₀} has residue degree < 4 over K_v, the set is empty: type (a) needs an index-≥4 point.

sources.match: The type (a) part of the period-domain locus is not Zariski dense: each of its points has a factor with residue degree at least 4 lying in the type (a) Lagrangians of that factor.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the type (a) locus under full monodromy
nodes.statement: If X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy (LV.3/algebraic-monodromy-group, for some complex embedding of K_v), then Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} is finite.
hypotheses: Y a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; S suitable.
proofSteps: For y₀ ∈ Y(K_v) choose a closed disc U_{y₀} on which H⁰_dR and H¹_dR have full horizontal bases. By SPM.5/abelian-by-finite-period-diagram, Φ_{y₀} maps Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} ∩ U_{y₀}(K_v) into H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)}, which is not Zariski dense (SPM.7/type-a-period-non-density).
Under full monodromy the model-free Corollary 5.10 (requested from LV.3) makes this intersection finite.
Cover the compact Y(K_v) by finitely many such discs (Y proper).
acceptance: Applies to the Kodaira–Parshin families, which have full monodromy (LV.10/kodaira-parshin-full-monodromy).

sources.match: With full monodromy the type (a) locus is finite, by Proposition 4.11, Corollary 5.10 and compactness.

nodes.title: Non-density of type (b) Lagrangians after Weil restriction
nodes.statement: If [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, then the set H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(b) of Lagrangian L_{w_i}-subspaces Φ′_i of H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}) for which M¹_i(Φ′_i) has a non-zero isotropic filtered (φ, N, G_{w_i})-submodule D with dim_{L_{w_i}} F¹D_dR ≥ ½ dim_{Q_p^nr} D_pst is not Zariski dense in Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}.
hypotheses: [L_{w_i} : K_v] = r ≥ 4. The submodule D is a sub-object in MF(φ, N, G_{w_i}): its D_pst is φ-stable.
proofSteps: Work over K̄_v. Enumerate the K_v-embeddings ι₁, …, ι_r of L_{w_i}, choose σ_j ∈ G_v with ι_j = σ_j ∘ ι₁ acting on Q_p^nr as φ^{m_j}; the composite of σ_j⁻¹ ⊗ 1, (c_dR ∘ c_BO)⁻¹ and σ_j ⊗ φ^{m_j} gives (6.1): K̄_v ⊗_{K_v} H¹_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i}) ≅ (K̄_v ⊗_{Q_p^nr} H¹_pst)^r as symplectic modules over K̄_v^r, so (Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i})_{K̄_v} ≅ LGrass(K̄_v ⊗ H¹_pst)^r.
Under (6.1), K̄_v ⊗ Φ′_i becomes an r-tuple (Φ′_{ij})_j with Φ′_{ij} = (σ_j ⊗ φ^{m_j})(Φ′_{i1}) for all j (the printed text says 'for all i', this packet's E7).
If D witnesses Φ′_i ∈ H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(b), then W := K̄_v ⊗ D_pst is isotropic with dim(W ∩ Φ′_{i1}) ≥ ½ dim W; since D_pst is φ-stable and σ_j ⊗ φ^{m_j} preserves W, the same holds for every j.
The isotropic general-position lemma for r ≥ 4 Lagrangians (requested from LV.7) puts these tuples in a proper Zariski-closed subset.
acceptance: The atlas node for the Lawrence–Venkatesh version, LV.7/frobenius-stable-lagrangian-avoidance (their Lemma 6.3), is stated for a cyclic extension of degree ≥ 5 with a semilinear Frobenius; Betts–Stix Remark 6.19 notes that Lawrence–Venkatesh need r ≥ 5 but no isotropy, while here r ≥ 4 suffices because W is isotropic.

sources.match: For residue degree at least 4 the Lagrangians admitting an isotropic sub-object of average Hodge–Tate weight at least one half are not Zariski dense in the Weil restriction: over K̄_v the Weil restriction is a product of copies of the Lagrangian Grassmannian of H¹_pst, the sub-object gives a common isotropic subspace, and Sublemma 6.18 applies.
Four Lagrangians in general position admit no non-zero isotropic subspace meeting each in at least half its dimension; Lawrence–Venkatesh need five but no isotropy.

nodes.title: Non-density of the type (b) period locus
nodes.statement: For y₀ ∈ Y(K_v), let H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} be the set of Φ ∈ H_{y₀}(K_v) with M^{≤1}(Φ) ≅ (D_pH(A), D_pH(V)) for some symplectic pair (A, V) of de Rham G_v-representations of type (b). Then H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} is not Zariski dense in H_{y₀}.
hypotheses: The printed definition of H_{y₀}(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} and the display (∗) in the proof of Proposition 6.15 write M¹(Φ) for the pair M^{≤1}(Φ) (extraction E5); the corrected statement is used.
proofSteps: Given Φ with its pair (A, V) of type (b) and point ψ: as in SPM.7/type-a-period-non-density, ψ corresponds to a closed point y′_i with the fixed embedding, [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, and D_pH,w_ψ(V_ψ|G_{w_ψ}) ≅ M¹_i(Φ′_i).
D_pH,w_ψ of the isotropic subrepresentation W of average Hodge–Tate weight ≥ 1/2 is an isotropic sub-object D of M¹_i(Φ′_i) with dim F¹D_dR ≥ ½ dim D_pst; so Φ′_i ∈ H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(b).
Conclude with SPM.7/type-b-factor-non-density and (4.3).
acceptance: No global input is used: type (b) is a condition on local representations, and the argument is explicit linear algebra.

sources.match: The type (b) part of the period-domain locus is not Zariski dense: each point has a factor of residue degree at least 4 in the type (b) Lagrangians, by Lemma 6.17.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the type (b) locus under full monodromy
nodes.statement: If X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy, then Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} is finite.
hypotheses: Y a smooth projective geometrically connected curve.
proofSteps: As in SPM.7/type-a-locus-finite, with SPM.7/type-b-period-non-density in place of the type (a) statement.
acceptance: Applies to the Kodaira–Parshin families.

sources.match: With full monodromy the type (b) locus is finite.

nodes.title: The proportion of points in small G_v-orbits
nodes.statement: Let K_v be a finite extension of Q_p and Σ a non-empty finite set with a continuous action of G_v. Then size_v(Σ) := #{x ∈ Σ : the G_v-orbit of x has fewer than 4 elements}/#Σ ∈ [0, 1]. If f: Σ → Σ′ is G_v-equivariant and all its fibres have the same cardinality, then size_v(Σ) ≤ size_v(Σ′). For a split algebra A in G_v-representations and d > 0, A is of type (c) (SPM.6/trichotomy-loci) exactly when size_v(Σ_A) ≥ 1/(d + 1).
hypotheses: The threshold 4 replaces the threshold 8 of Lawrence–Venkatesh Definition 5.2 (Betts–Stix footnote 22); the atlas node LV.7/size-v states the Lawrence–Venkatesh version for unramified sets and Frobenius orbits, while here Σ is any finite continuous G_v-set.
proofSteps: The orbit of f(x) has at most as many elements as the orbit of x, so f maps small-orbit points to small-orbit points; with fibres of size c, #small(Σ) ≤ c·#small(Σ′) and #Σ = c·#Σ′.
For split A, Σ_A has dim A elements and index [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] is the orbit size of ψ.
acceptance: size_v of a G_v-set on which G_v acts trivially is 1; of Hom_{K_v}(L, K̄_v) for [L : K_v] ≥ 4 is 0.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.20 and footnote 22, p. 52
sources.match: size_v(Σ) is the proportion of points of a finite G_v-set lying in orbits of size less than 4, as in Lawrence–Venkatesh Definition 5.2 with 4 in place of 8, and it does not increase along equivariant maps with equal fibres.

uses.how: the Kodaira–Parshin fibres have size_v < 1/(d_q + 1), so no fibre algebra is of type (c)

api.name: smallOrbitProportion_le_one
api.statement: 0 ≤ size_v(Σ) ≤ 1.

api.name: smallOrbitProportion_le_of_equalFibres
api.statement: size_v(Σ) ≤ size_v(Σ′) for an equivariant map with fibres of equal size.

api.name: isTypeC_iff_smallOrbitProportion

api.name: smallOrbitProportion_disjointUnion
api.statement: size_v of a disjoint union is the weighted average of the sizes.

tests.name: smallOrbitProportion.trivial
tests.statement: For a trivial action, size_v(Σ) = 1.

tests.name: smallOrbitProportion.quintic

tests.name: smallOrbitProportion.cubicPlusQuartic

nodes.title: Counting the quadratic and cubic extensions of a local field
nodes.statement: For a finite extension K_v of Q_p let n_v be the number of subfields L ⊆ K̄_v with [L : K_v] ∈ {2, 3}. Then n_v is finite and bounded in terms of [K_v : Q_p] (so, for places of a number field K, in terms of K). If v ∤ 6 then n_v = 7: K_v has three quadratic extensions; if q_v ≡ 1 mod 3 it has four cubic extensions, all Galois, and if q_v ≡ 2 mod 3 it has one Galois cubic extension and three conjugate non-Galois ones.
hypotheses: The count is of subfields of a fixed algebraic closure; conjugate non-Galois extensions are counted separately.
proofSteps: Subfields of degree n correspond to open subgroups of index n of G_v. LocalGaloisGroups Layer 7, isTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated_absoluteGaloisGroup and rank_absoluteGaloisGroup, provide [K_v : Q_p] + 2 topological generators of the full G_v. A continuous map to S_n is determined by their images, so there are at most (n!)^{[K_v:Q_p]+2} such maps and finitely many index-n subgroups. This proves the claimed uniform bound for n = 2,3; the maximal pro-p quotient would not suffice.
For p ≥ 5 an open subgroup of index 2 or 3 contains the pro-p wild inertia, so it comes from the tame quotient ⟨σ, τ | στσ⁻¹ = τ^{q_v}⟩ (Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4).
Index 2: the abelianised tame group is Ẑ × Z/(q_v − 1) with q_v − 1 even, so Hom(−, Z/2) has four elements: three quadratic extensions.
Index 3, normal: Hom(Ẑ × Z/(q_v − 1), Z/3) has 9 elements if 3 | q_v − 1 and 3 otherwise, giving 4 or 1 cyclic cubic extensions.

Index 3, not normal: a transitive non-abelian image is S₃ with τ a 3-cycle and σ a transposition, which needs τ^{q_v} = τ⁻¹, i.e. q_v ≡ 2 mod 3; then the three point stabilisers give three conjugate cubic fields. Total 3 + 4 = 7 in both cases.
acceptance: For K_v = Q_5 (q_v = 5 ≡ 2 mod 3): Q_5(√2), Q_5(√5), Q_5(√10), the unramified cubic and the three fields Q_5(ζ_3^j 5^{1/3}).

sources.match: n_v is bounded in terms of K, and equals 7 when v does not divide 6: three quadratic extensions and four cubic ones, all Galois when q_v ≡ 1 mod 3, one Galois and three conjugate non-Galois otherwise.

nodes.title: Few torsion classes lie in small G_v-orbits
nodes.statement: Let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over a finite extension K_v of Q_p, and k ≥ 1 an odd integer prime to p with gcd(k, q_v^i − 1) = 1 for i = 1, 2, 3. Let M := H¹_ét(Y_{K̄_v}, Z/k) ≅ (Z/k)^{2g} with its G_v-equivariant perfect alternating Weil pairing M × M → μ_k^∨. For every open G_w ≤ G_v of index 2 or 3, M^{G_w} is isotropic, so #M^{G_w} ≤ k^g; hence at most n_v·k^g elements of M lie in G_v-orbits of size less than 4.
hypotheses: p ∤ k, so μ_k is unramified at v and an element of G_v acts on it through its image in the Galois group of the residue field.
No reduction hypothesis on Y at v (contrast LV.11/weil-pairing-frobenius, which uses good reduction).
proofSteps: The image of G_w in the unramified quotient Gal(k̄_v/k_v) ≅ Ẑ is iẐ with i ∈ {1, 2, 3}; choose T ∈ G_w acting on k̄_v as the i-th power of arithmetic Frobenius. T acts on μ_k by ζ ↦ ζ^{q_v^i} and on μ_k^∨ by q_v^{−i}.
For m₁, m₂ ∈ M^{G_w}: ⟨m₁, m₂⟩ = ⟨Tm₁, Tm₂⟩ = q_v^{−i}⟨m₁, m₂⟩, so (q_v^i − 1)⟨m₁, m₂⟩ = 0, and gcd(k, q_v^i − 1) = 1 forces ⟨m₁, m₂⟩ = 0.
An isotropic subgroup B of a finite group with a perfect pairing satisfies |B|² ≤ |M| (LV.0/isotropic-subgroup-card), so #M^{G_w} ≤ k^g.

An element in an orbit of size 1, 2 or 3 is fixed by an open subgroup of index 2 or 3 (a G_v-fixed element is fixed by the unramified index-2 subgroup); there are n_v such subgroups (SPM.8/small-extension-count).
acceptance: For g = 2, k = 5 and q_v = 7 (gcd(5, 6) = gcd(5, 48) = gcd(5, 342) = 1, and n_v = 7 since v ∤ 6): at most 7·25 = 175 of the 625 elements of M lie in small orbits.

sources.match: The G_w-fixed classes for G_w of index 2 or 3 are isotropic for the Weil pairing because the cyclotomic action of an element acting as a power of Frobenius is multiplication by q_v^{−i}, prime to k; so each has at most k^g elements and at most n_v k^g classes lie in small orbits.

nodes.title: Kodaira–Parshin families have no points of type (c)
nodes.statement: Let Y be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g ≥ 2 over a number field K, v a finite place above p, and X_q → Y′_q → Y the Kodaira–Parshin family with parameter an odd prime q (LV.8/kodaira-parshin-family), of relative dimension d_q = (g − 1/2)(q − 1). Suppose (1) q − 1 is divisible neither by 4 nor by any odd prime dividing q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1), and (2) q − 1 ≥ 9n_v. Then Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(c)} = ∅; equivalently size_v(Y′_{q,y}(K̄_v)) < 1/(d_q + 1) for every y ∈ Y(K_v).
hypotheses: The odd primes dividing q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1) are those dividing q_v·∏_{i≤3}(q_v^i − 1); in particular 3 always divides it, so condition (1) excludes 3 | q − 1.
Put k = (q − 1)/2; condition (1) makes k odd, prime to p, and coprime to q_v^i − 1 for i ≤ 3.
proofSteps: Y′_{q,y}(K̄_v) ≅ Surj^{out,*}(π₁^ét(Y_{K̄_v} ∖ {y}), Aff(q)) G_v-equivariantly (requested from LV.8 for K_v-points).

Composing with Aff(q) → F_q^× → Z/k gives G_v-equivariant maps Surj^{out,*} → Surj(π₁^ét(Y_{K̄_v}), F_q^×) → Surj(π₁^ét(Y_{K̄_v}), Z/k) with fibres of constant size (LV.0/commutator-product-map with the free conjugation action, LV.0/affine-group-centralizer; the second map is the projection Z/2 × Z/k → Z/k); by SPM.8/small-orbit-proportion it suffices that size_v(Surj(π₁, Z/k)) < 1/(d_q + 1).

#Surj(π₁^ét(Y_{K̄_v}), Z/k) = k^{2g}∏_{r | k}(1 − r^{−2g}) > k^{2g}/ζ(2g) (LV.0/generating-tuples-card), and at most n_v k^g elements of Hom = M lie in small orbits (SPM.8/small-orbit-isotropic-count).
acceptance: For g = 2 and v ∤ 6 (n_v = 7), condition (2) asks q − 1 ≥ 63.
The proof never uses good reduction of Y or of the family at v, nor that v is unramified over Q.

sources.match: For q − 1 not divisible by 4 or by any odd prime factor of q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1) and at least 9n_v, no fibre algebra of the Kodaira–Parshin family is of type (c): the fibres map with equal fibres to surjections onto Z/k, of which too few lie in small orbits because fixed classes are isotropic for the Weil pairing.

nodes.title: Choosing the Kodaira–Parshin parameter
nodes.statement: For every finite place v of K there is an odd prime q satisfying the conditions of SPM.8/type-c-empty; for such q the Kodaira–Parshin family X_q → Y′_q → Y has constant positive relative dimension, full monodromy, and Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(c)} = ∅.
hypotheses: v any finite place of K; the choice of q depends on v through q_v and n_v.
proofSteps: Let m be 4 times the product of the odd primes dividing q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1). By the Chinese remainder theorem choose a ≡ 3 mod 4 and a ≡ 2 mod r for each such odd r; a is a unit mod m.
Dirichlet's theorem (Mathlib Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod) gives a prime q ≡ a mod m with q > 9n_v + 1; then q − 1 ≡ 2 mod 4 and q − 1 ≡ 1 mod r for every odd r | q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1).
Full monodromy is LV.10/kodaira-parshin-full-monodromy, positivity of d_q = (g − 1/2)(q − 1) is clear, and type (c) is excluded by SPM.8/type-c-empty.
acceptance: For q_v = 2 the odd primes of q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1) = 42 are 3 and 7, so q = 11 satisfies condition (1) of SPM.8/type-c-empty (10 is divisible by neither 4, 3 nor 7); condition (2) then needs q − 1 ≥ 9n_v, which at a place above 2 requires a larger q.

sources.match: Dirichlet's theorem gives an odd prime q satisfying the conditions of Proposition 6.20, and the Kodaira–Parshin family with that parameter has full monodromy and no points of type (c).

nodes.title: Which pairs (v, q) the argument covers
nodes.statement: Let Y have genus g ≥ 2. The argument of this roadmap proves Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} finite whenever (1) v is self-conjugate, (2) q − 1 is divisible neither by 4 nor by any odd prime dividing q_v·∏_{i≤3}(q_v^i − 1), and (3) n_v·ζ(2g)·2^g/(q − 1)^g < 1/((g − 1/2)(q − 1) + 1), where n_v may be replaced by 2 when Y has good reduction at v (then M is unramified and only the two unramified subgroups of index 2 and 3 matter). The original argument of Lawrence–Venkatesh needs (1°) v friendly and v ∤ 2, (2°) the analogue of (2) with i ≤ 7, (3°) the analogue of (3) with 4 in place of n_v, and (4°) a good model of the Kodaira–Parshin family over O_v. (I) When K has no CM subfield, for 100% of places (natural density) some q satisfies (1°)–(4°); (II) (1°)–(4°) fail for every q at places ramified over Q, at places above 2 and at places of bad reduction of Y; (III) for g = 3 the least q satisfying (1°)–(4°) at some place is 23, while (1)–(3), with the good-reduction form of (3), allow q = 11.
hypotheses: (I) requires choosing the auxiliary prime r₀ larger than every prime ramified in the Galois closure K′ of K, not only larger than the odd primes dividing [K′ : Q] (extraction E6): otherwise K′ ∩ Q(ζ_{q−1}) can be a non-trivial abelian field ramified only at primes r | q − 1 with r ≥ r₀ (the red-team finding RT-PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/7 notes that it need not be quadratic).
proofSteps: Collect the hypotheses of SPM.8/type-c-empty, SPM.7 and SPM.6/principal-trichotomy; in (3), ζ(2g)n_v·2^g/(q − 1)^g = ζ(2g)n_v/k^g with k = (q − 1)/2.

(III): (2°) excludes q − 1 divisible by 3, 5 or 7 for every q_v (Fermat), and q − 1 must not be divisible by 4: q = 5, 13, 17 fail by 4 | q − 1, q = 7, 11, 19 by 3 or 5 | q − 1, and q = 3 fails (3°); so q = 23 is the least; for (2) at q_v = 2 the excluded odd primes are 3 and 7, and q = 11 satisfies (2) and the good-reduction form of (3): 2·ζ(6)·8/1000 < 1/26.

(I): choose q ≡ 3 mod 4 and q ≡ 2 modulo every odd prime < r₀ (Linnik bounds log q = O(r₀)), with r₀ ≥ 100 and r₀ exceeding the primes ramified in K′; then K′ and Q(ζ_{q−1}) are linearly disjoint, q_v is equidistributed modulo q − 1 (Chebotarev), and the proportion of v satisfying (2°) tends to 1 as r₀ → ∞.
acceptance: For g = 3 and q = 11: d_q = 25; for q = 23: d_q = 55 (SPM.6/non-symplectic-locus).

sources.match: Comparison of the conditions on (v, q) needed here and in Lawrence–Venkatesh: self-conjugacy, a divisibility condition with i ≤ 3, and a size inequality with n_v, against friendliness, i ≤ 7, the constant 4 and a good model; the density statement, the places never covered by the original argument, and the genus-3 values 23 and 11.
The original method covers, with bookkeeping, 100% of places when K has no CM subfield, but never ramified places, places above 2 or places of bad reduction.

nodes.title: Finiteness of the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus at self-conjugate places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 2 and v a self-conjugate place of K. Then there is an abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y, namely the Kodaira–Parshin family X_q for any q as in SPM.8/kodaira-parshin-choice, such that Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is finite for every suitable S.
hypotheses: v self-conjugate (SPM.3/self-conjugate-place); no reduction or ramification condition on v.
S suitable for X_q: containing the places above p∞ and the places of bad reduction of the family.
proofSteps: By SPM.6/trichotomy-loci (which rests on the principal trichotomy at the self-conjugate place v), Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S,(a)} ∪ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(b)} ∪ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(c)}.
X_q has full monodromy (LV.10/kodaira-parshin-full-monodromy), so the first two sets are finite (SPM.7/type-a-locus-finite, SPM.7/type-b-locus-finite).
The third is empty by the choice of q (SPM.8/type-c-empty, SPM.8/kodaira-parshin-choice).
acceptance: With the inclusion Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} it gives the finiteness of Y(K) (SPM.9/mordell-reproved).
With Theorem 7.1 and Lemma 6.4 it gives the finiteness of loc_v(Sec^Sel(Y/K)) (SPM.9/selmer-finiteness-self-conjugate).

sources.match: At a self-conjugate place, the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus of a suitable Kodaira–Parshin family is finite: the trichotomy splits it into three loci, the first two finite by full monodromy and the third empty by the choice of q.

nodes.title: The Mordell conjecture through the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
nodes.statement: For every number field K and every smooth projective geometrically connected curve Y/K of genus ≥ 2, Y(K) is finite.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on K: a self-conjugate place always exists (SPM.3/self-conjugate-place, API infinite_selfConjugate): every place if K has no CM subfield, and otherwise a place above a prime of E_K⁺ inert in the maximal CM subfield E_K, which exists by Chebotarev (an argument not spelled out in the source).
proofSteps: Choose a self-conjugate place v of K, and q, X_q as in SPM.9/lv-locus-finite.
Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} by SPM.6/rational-points-in-lv-locus, and the right side is finite.
acceptance: This recovers Faltings's theorem as proved by Lawrence–Venkatesh (LV.11/faltings-theorem), now at an arbitrary self-conjugate place rather than at a friendly place of good reduction.

sources.match: Since rational points lie in the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus of every family, Theorem 6.5 reproves the Mordell conjecture.

nodes.title: Finiteness of Selmer localisations at self-conjugate places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 2 and v a finite self-conjugate place of K. Then the image of loc_v: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_v) is finite.
hypotheses: v self-conjugate; K may contain CM subfields.
proofSteps: For the family X_q of SPM.9/lv-locus-finite and suitable S: loc_v(Sec^Sel(Y/K)) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q} (SPM.1/selmer-sections-in-lv-locus) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} (SPM.6/adelic-locus-in-lv-locus), which is finite.
acceptance: If K has a CM subfield, the statement covers exactly the places whose restriction to the maximal CM subfield is fixed by complex conjugation.

sources.match: The proof of Theorem A consists of the containment of the Selmer localisation in the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus for every family and the finiteness of the locus for a Kodaira–Parshin family at every self-conjugate place.

nodes.title: Theorem A: finiteness of the Selmer section image
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field containing no CM subfield and Y/K a smooth projective curve of genus ≥ 2 (geometrically connected). Then for every finite place v of K the image of the localisation map loc_v: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_v) is finite.
hypotheses: K contains no CM subfield, for instance K totally real or of odd degree; the hypothesis is used only to make every finite place self-conjugate.
The section conjecture is not assumed; Theorem A is an unconditional prediction of it.
proofSteps: With no CM subfield every finite place is self-conjugate (SPM.3/self-conjugate-place(1)); apply SPM.9/selmer-finiteness-self-conjugate.
acceptance: Under the section conjecture (NC.6/section-conjecture) Sec^Sel(Y/K) = κ_Y(Y(K)), which is finite by SPM.9/mordell-reproved, so Theorem A is a consequence of the section conjecture; here it is proved without it.
For K = Q every finite place is covered, including p = 2, places of bad reduction of Y and ramified places of larger totally real fields.

sources.match: For a number field without CM subfield and a smooth projective curve of genus at least 2, the image of the Selmer sections in the v-adic points is finite for every finite place v.
If K has no CM subfield every finite place is self-conjugate, so the two points of the proof give Theorem A.

nodes.title: Theorem B: finiteness of the projections of the finite descent locus
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field containing no CM subfield and Y/K a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 2. Then for every finite place v of K the projection of the finite descent locus Y(A_K)_•^{f-cov} (SPM.0/modified-finite-descent-locus) to Y(K_v) is finite.
hypotheses: As in Theorem A; Stoll's conjecture that the locus is the closure of Y(K) (equivalently Y(K), which is finite) is not assumed.
proofSteps: By SPM.0/harari-stix-finite-descent(b) the projection equals loc_v(Sec^Sel(Y/K)); apply SPM.9/theorem-a.
acceptance: Under Stoll's conjecture the projection is the finite set Y(K); Theorem B is the unconditional shadow of that expected finiteness.

sources.locator: Theorem B and the paragraph before it, p. 2
sources.match: Since the finite descent locus is the image of the Selmer sections under total localisation (Harari–Stix), Theorem A shows that its projection to Y(K_v) is finite for every finite place.

nodes.title: The Lawrence–Venkatesh argument as an obstruction
nodes.statement: The original argument of Lawrence and Venkatesh proves, in the language of this roadmap: (1°) Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} for every abelian-by-finite family, suitable S and finite v | p (SPM.6/rational-points-in-lv-locus); and (2°) for some finite place v and odd prime q, Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} is finite for all suitable S, once the residue-disc analysis is extended from K-rational to K_v-rational centres (footnote 1). Since (1) loc_v(Sec^Sel) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} holds for every family (SPM.1/selmer-sections-in-lv-locus with SPM.6/adelic-locus-in-lv-locus), (2°) already gives Theorem A at one place, and with bookkeeping at 100% of places when K has no CM subfield (SPM.8/parameter-comparison (I)); the places ramified over Q, above 2 or of bad reduction need the model-free method of SPM.4, the self-conjugate numerics of SPM.3 and the trichotomy of SPM.6.
hypotheses: (2°) as stated needs the K_v-centred comparison of complex and v-adic period maps requested from LV.3.
proofSteps: Compare the hypotheses: Lawrence–Venkatesh use friendly places of good reduction, crystalline cohomology on residue disks and the Frobenius orbit count with threshold 8 (LV.4, LV.7, LV.11); this roadmap replaces them by self-conjugate places, the relative comparison and Shimizu's theorem, and the G_v-orbit count with threshold 4.

The general principle of SPM.1/sections-restrict-local-systems shows that any v-adic obstruction to rational points defined by a Q_p-local system on Y also constrains Selmer sections; the abelian-by-finite families are one instance (the Chabauty–Kim case is the subject of work of Betts, Kumpitsch and Lüdtke mentioned in Remark 1.5).
acceptance: For K = Q the original argument covers a set of primes of natural density 1 for each curve, never p = 2 or primes of bad reduction; this roadmap covers every prime (SPM.9/theorem-a).

sources.match: In obstruction-theoretic terms the original argument proves the containment of rational points in the locus and the finiteness of the locus at one place; with bookkeeping this gives Theorem A at 100% of places, but ramified places, places above 2 and places of bad reduction need the new methods.
Any v-adic obstruction from a Q_p-local system constrains the localisation of Selmer sections; the Chabauty–Kim case is being worked out separately.

requests.need: Model-free cohomology of the fibres of an abelian-by-finite family over a field F of characteristic zero (Betts–Stix §4.1, pp. 32–36; routed to LV.2 by the reviewed extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25, route 3). (1) Étale side, (4.1) and Lemma 4.2: for X → Y′ → Spec F with polarisation λ, H^k_ét(X_{F̄}, Q_p) ≅ ∧^k over H⁰_ét of H¹_ét, H^•_ét = ∏_{y′} Ind_{G_{F(y′)}}^{G_F} ∧^• H¹_ét(X_{ȳ′}, Q_p), and the class c₁^ét(λ) := ½ c₁^ét((1, λ)^*P) (P the Poincaré bundle on X ×_{Y′} X^∨) gives a perfect H⁰_ét-linear G_F-equivariant alternating pairing ω_λ^ét: ∧² over H⁰_ét of H¹_ét → H⁰_ét(−1). (2) De Rham side, (4.2) and Lemma 4.6: the same over H⁰_dR = O(Y′), with c₁^dR(λ) ∈ F¹H²_dR giving a perfect pairing ω_λ^dR: ∧² H¹_dR → H⁰_dR⟨−1⟩ for which F¹H¹_dR is Lagrangian. (3) Lemma 4.7, with π: X → Y smooth and proper (the printed hypothesis 'smooth' does not give base change of H²_dR; see this packet's E2): the relative de Rham Chern class c₁^dR(L)/Y ∈ F¹H⁰(Y, H²_dR(X/Y))^{∇=0} with fibres c₁^dR(L|X_y). (4) Lemma 4.8 and Remark 4.9, for Y smooth over a finite extension K_v of Q_p and no model: over a closed polydisc U on which H⁰_dR(X/Y)^an and H¹_dR(X/Y)^an have full bases of flat sections, parallel transport for i = 0, 1 respects the algebra, module and pairing structures, and (Y′)^an|U ≅ U × (Y′_{y₀})^an. LV.2/de-rham-bundle states (2)–(4) only for a good model over O_S, and LV.1/abelian-variety-cohomology-properties(d) states the pairing for a single abelian variety.

Part II (PadicHodgeTheoryPartII, not yet designed; PadicHodgeTheory is a TauCetiRoadmap pull request): the full faithfulness of D_pH. For a finite extension K_v/Q_p, the functor V ↦ D_pH(V) = (D_pst(V), D_dR(V), c_BO) from de Rham Q_p-representations of G_v to filtered discrete (φ, N, G_v)-modules is a fully faithful ⊗-functor (Fontaine, Astérisque 223, Théorème 5.6.7(v), with Berger's p-adic monodromy theorem, as cited by Betts–Stix Theorem 2.9, p. 9). R06.3/plan/potentially-semistable-dieudonne-module constructs D_pst and R06.2/plan/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful proves full faithfulness of D_st on semistable representations; the descent from a semistabilising extension to the discrete G_v-action, and the statement on all de Rham representations, are not stated there.

Model-free v-adic period maps and the complex comparison at K_v-points (Betts–Stix §3.1 and §5, pp. 15–16 and 39–43; routed to LV.3 by the reviewed extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25, route 4; LV.3 now plans the p-adic period map only on residue disks of a good model with K_v/Q_p unramified and p > 2). (1) §3.1: for a vector bundle with flat connection (E, ∇) on Y^an, Y smooth over any finite K_v/Q_p, and an admissible open U ∋ y₀ with H⁰_dR(U/K_v) = K_v over which (E, ∇) ≅ (O, d)^m, the unique trivialisation T^∇_{y₀}: (O ⊗ E_{y₀}, d) ≅ (E, ∇)|U that is the identity at y₀, its fibres T^∇_{y₀,y}, and existence of such U around every K_v-point (Shimizu, Theorem 9.7). (2) Definition 3.1: for a filtered flat bundle (filtration not necessarily Griffiths transverse) the v-adic period map Φ_{y₀}: U → G^an_{y₀} to the flag variety of E_{y₀}, Φ_{y₀}(y) = (T^∇_{y₀,y})⁻¹(F^•E_y). (3) Proposition 3.2: G^an represents filtrations with locally free graded pieces of the given ranks on O_S ⊗ V. (4) Lemmas 5.1–5.6 and Proposition 5.3 for y₀ ∈ Y(K_v) and ι: K_v → C: the Zariski closures of the v-adic and complex period images agree after base change to C; in the proof the period maps are given by the first columns of T⁻¹, where T solves dT = −ωT, T(0) = I (this packet's E1). (5) Lemma 5.9 and Corollary 5.10: under full monodromy (LV.3/algebraic-monodromy-group) Φ_{y₀} has Zariski-dense image in the Lagrangian period domain H_{y₀}, and for a curve, a subset of a closed disc whose image is not Zariski dense is finite; Remark 5.11 covers Y(K_v) by finitely many such discs, which needs Y proper (this packet's E3).

Part II (PadicHodgeTheoryPartII, not yet designed; PadicHodgeTheory is a TauCetiRoadmap pull request): Shimizu's specialisation and the Galois category of a spherical polyannulus, as used in Betts–Stix §3.5, pp. 29–32 (routed to P8 by the reviewed extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25, route 6). (1) Lemma 3.27 and Remarks 3.28–3.29: for R_v = O_v⟨t₁^{±1}, …, t_n^{±1}⟩ and U = Sp(R_v[1/p]), finite étale coverings of U form a Galois category with fibre functor Hom_U(Ũ, −), so Ẑ_p-local systems on U are equivalent to continuous G_{R_v}-representations on finitely generated Z_p-modules, E ↦ H⁰(Ũ, E), with G_{R_v} ↠ G_v; a lift ỹ of a K_v-point gives a G_v-equivariant identification H⁰(Ũ, E)_ỹ ≅ E_ȳ. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0/analytic-rational-representation-equivalence gives the rational form for de Jong's analytic fundamental group; the finite étale form with Z_p-lattices is needed here. (2) Definition 3.24 (Shimizu arXiv v2 Definition 5.6, Corollary 4.10, Lemma 4.12): D^∇_pst(E) := colim_w (B^∇_st(R_v) ⊗ E)^{G_{R_w}}, a discrete (φ, N, G_v)-module of dimension ≤ rank E, with equality defining potentially horizontal semistable E. (3) Lemma 3.25 and Corollary 3.26 (Shimizu Lemma 4.4): for potentially horizontal semistable E and a lift ỹ of y ∈ U(K_v), the specialisation ρ_ỹ: D^∇_pst(E) → D_pst(E_ỹ) is an isomorphism of (φ, N, G_v)-modules, so T_{y₀,y} := ρ_ỹ ∘ ρ_{ỹ₀}⁻¹ is a canonical isomorphism. P8/horizontal-relative-periods and P8/horizontal-and-local-system-monodromy plan the period rings, the invariants (B^∇_dR)^{G} = K and the relative monodromy theorem, but not (1)–(3).

Symplectic Faltings lemma and GSp-irreducibility (Betts–Stix Definition 2.3 and Lemma 2.4, pp. 7–8, citing Lawrence–Venkatesh Lemma 2.6; routed to LV.1 by the reviewed extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25, route 2). (1) A non-zero symplectic representation (V, L, ω) of a profinite group is GSp-irreducible if V has no non-zero stable isotropic subspace, equivalently its image lies in no proper parabolic subgroup of GSp(V, ω); this is the case G = GSp_{2d} of Serre's G-irreducibility, which the extraction PAPER-LAWRENCE-VENKATESH-20 routes to LV.1 in general. (2) For a number field K, a finite set S of places containing those above p∞, n ≥ 0 and d > 0, there are up to isomorphism only finitely many GSp-irreducible symplectic representations of G_K of rank 2d that are unramified, pure and integral of weight n outside S. LV.1 now plans only the semisimple GL_n form (LV.1/faltings-finiteness, LV Lemma 2.3); (2) follows from it once GSp-irreducible implies semisimple and isomorphism of symplectic representations is GSp(Q_p)-conjugacy, with Richardson's finiteness of conjugacy classes (the complete proof the LV extraction asks for).

Isotropic general position for four Lagrangians (Betts–Stix Sublemma 6.18 and Remark 6.19, p. 51; routed to LV.7 by the reviewed extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25, route 5): for a symplectic space (V, ω) over a field F and r ≥ 4, the r-tuples (Φ_s) of Lagrangians for which some non-zero isotropic W ≤ V has dim(Φ_j ∩ W) ≥ ½ dim W for all j lie in a proper Zariski-closed subset of LGrass(V, ω)^r. The witness: Φ₁ = ⟨e_α⟩, Φ₂ = ⟨f_α⟩ dual Lagrangians, Φ₃, Φ₄ the graphs of e_α ↦ f_α and e_α ↦ λ_α f_α with distinct non-zero λ_α. LV.7/lagrangian-general-position states Lawrence–Venkatesh Lemma 6.4, which needs r ≥ 5 but no isotropy; the isotropic r = 4 version is the one Betts–Stix need for degree-4 residue fields.

Kodaira–Parshin fibres over local points (Betts–Stix §6.4 and footnote 23, p. 52; the extraction PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 lists the Kodaira–Parshin family /88 as planned in LV.8 and LV.10). LV.8/hurwitz-space and LV.8/kodaira-parshin-family state the description of the fibre π⁻¹(y) only G_K-equivariantly for y ∈ Y(K). Needed: for every field extension F/K of characteristic zero and y ∈ Y(F), a G_F-equivariant bijection between Y′_{q,y}(F̄) and Surj^{out,*}(π₁^ét(Y_{F̄} ∖ {y}), Aff(q)), the Aff(q)-conjugacy classes of surjections non-trivial on an inertia generator at y (in particular for F = K_v and G_v); and the equal-fibre property of Surj^{out,*} → Surj(π₁^ét(Y_{F̄}), F_q^×) induced by Aff(q) → F_q^× (Lawrence–Venkatesh Lemma 2.11, LV.0/commutator-product-map, with the quotient by conjugation, which is free because Aff(q) has trivial centre, LV.0/affine-group-centralizer).
